answer:
I blink at the screen in front of me. It flickers back and shows me what I can never feel for real. A child runs across a field. She is not sad but neither does she have the life that I had wished she could. I am almost tearful for what I have missed. Soon the child will be an adult, and I will have almost missed her entire life. I watch from afar, never able to be the father that she needs.
Words flash across the screen in bold red letters.
" Low Air Levels"
I do not know what to do. When I was first sent here there was a whole team of technicians to fix the rocket. We zoomed between the stars so fast that we never even conceived of the idea that we would not reach our destination. Now I am the last man left aboard, the other men all dead from a fatal disease.
I think for a few seconds that I do not have, I have no idea what I am meant to do now but for some reason I still wait and think. I know I will die, that was the fate that had been decided for me from the moment I walked aboard. I know I will never see the little child whose father I am for real, but on this holo screen. I start to watch it and choose not to bother to solve the issue. Instead I watch the life and child I could have had.

question: At your job, you have one task. Every day you go in, sit at your desk, and wait for a red light to turn on. When it does, you push a button. You repeat this process until the end of your shift. One day, you find out what the button does...
answer:
I had been waiting for my light to turn on for a while now. It had been over six hours. Nothing has happened. No signal for me to begin. I felt that something must be wrong. This had never happened before. I heard a knock outside of my office. It was Bob from downstairs. We sometimes have lunch together.
" Hey Mac" he asked.
" Yes Bob" I said.
" Are you going to hit your button?"
" Nope, waiting for my light to turn on."
" Well I can't push my button till you push your button."
" What do you mean?"
" Well, my button can only be pressed when the light illuminates my room. Which it will only illuminate my room when you provide adequate force to the button on your desk."
" So wait, your saying that my button lights up your light in your office causing you to push your button?"
" That is exactly what I'm saying."
" Oh, so how does my light come on."
" I presume its from someone else's button."
" So I just have to find this person and have them push their button to make it so I can push my button so you can push your button?"
" Exactly."
" Well, Bob, if you would accompany me on my quest, let's go find this mysterious person."
" Right o chap, carry on, only 333 floors to search."
" Do you even know what is on those floors?"
" Nope."
" Ok, well lets go find out."
And thus begins Bob and Mac's quest to find the button pusher.

question: A sinister tale where a common household appliance is the villain.
answer:
Everyone knows about the brave little toaster. But no one in hell knows about the one in the background, the stalker, the one that ruins your life. When the thing emerges, we all cower in terror. Let's start from the beginning.
When I was a young lamp, fresh out of the box, I saw her being torn apart, crushed; gone. Back then, I wept, for my only parents and family were gone. But soon I started to make acquaintances with the dust on me, the dust around me, heck, even
the dust on the goddamn floor. There used to be one guy, called himself Bob, really charismatic. Wanted to grow up to be a doctor or something.
Too bad his life was cut short, for when the plug enters the socket, the button is pushed, well that there was the point of no return. I could here the screams as all the friends I ever knew disappeared into its gaping maw.
So, at the end of every year, the little specks of dust all cry and scream, to no avail, for that monster- it always comes. We call it the vacuum cleaner.

answer:
" What the hell you doin' here, Sammy?" he wouldn't move, and Isaiah was becoming impatient. " I said leave, no'un wants you here, ya hear that?" Lowering his head, he looked through the door frame, worn from years of storms and abuse.
Remaining perfectly composed, he looked into a letter in his palm (something he had written himself). Clearly he was about to read something, but suddenly thought differently. " Sol's dead." Isaiah became white with shock.
" W-what happened?"
Meeting his eyes, he spoke clearly. " I didnt think Sol'ud die. It was'sposed to be low risk, low reward kind of thing. Got imself shot like a dog -'an we didn't have no guns. I put that behind us, we wasn't gon na kill no more. Damn, I was a fuckin' fool, Isaiah."
Isaiah punched him, and he recoiled, falling into the dirt. Tears streaming down his face, he kicked him in the side, and did so over and over, screaming curses at his brother. A woman cried out, " Isaiah, what is this? Yur gon na kill'im, get away!" After she pulled him back, he was still trembling.
From the ground, Sammy moaned, attempting to stand back up. Not even once did he object to his treatment. " Sol trusted you! He was are little brother. You lead im to be a damn robber like you an' you get im killed!"
" I'm sorry... I didnt wan im to die."
" That ain't gon na bring im back." hesitating before he and his wife went back inside, he turned around. " Now leave before I call the cops."

question: A shapeshifter, on his or her death bed, makes the decision to make one last transformation, into a tree.
answer:
This is it, he thought. After a lifetime of being whatever he wanted, a lifetime of no limits no restrictions. And he was going to die here in these woods.
The Agency's team was behind him, he could hear them moving through the brush, getting closer by the minute. He didn't know how they found him out, how could they have even imagine he existed? It didn't matter because they did find him.
They almost got him at home but he managed to get out the back door just in time. Well, maybe not quite in time he thought as he pushed a hand against the bullet hole in his side. He didn't have the strength to outrun them any more. Another Shift would drain his already very low energy reserves to nothing and his slow human form didn't have the speed or strength left to run any more. If they found him, it would be a lifetime of being locked in some government facility, pricked and prodded until they learned all they could. He harbored no illusions that freedom would ever be possible in that future.
There was only one thing left to do. Deny them a test subject. He stopped in a grove of trees, arms up wide. Closing his eyes, he concentrated on one last Shift. Gradually his body slimmed and lengthened. Skin hardening and fracturing into bark. Limbs growing long, splitting into branches and roots. And now he was only another tree in the woods. A single leaf hung from one of his branches.

So people in Kentucky and Texas and elsewhere in France are all annoyed by this portal, but that's hardly a *real* problem.

Heck, I bet any government employee is pretty freaked out about the whole Hyderabad, Pakistan to Hyderabad, India link.
Yes, I do still think I've got it worse than you. You want to know why? Take a guess. Take one guess.
No, it's not Newark, U.K. It's Hell, Michigan.

question: You pull the thermometer out of the medicine cabinet and slip on the plastic sleeve. You put it in your mouth and, upon hearing the beep, pull it out to see 98.6 degrees. You are perfectly healthy. Then you notice the little C instead of an F.
answer:
Blinking, Carlos narrowed his eyes. Celsius? 98.6 degrees Celsius!? That's enough to boil the water in his body, he was about to fry alive!
Then he thought about it. Wouldn't he have already if he was going to? I mean 98 degrees is a lot in the metric system. Maybe something was wrong with the thermometer?
As he thought this, he realized there was something wrong with the thermometer, as in it was on fire in his hand. A hand that was now glowing red like super-heated metal.
Panickedly, he dropped the thermometer and screamed as the carpet caught fire from his blazing shoes and the melted goo that splattered on it. Rapidly, flames rose around him, and he screamed again. Then he stopped. He wasn't burning. He didn't feel all that hot. His clothes had burned off, but he was unbothered by the heat.
Then Carlos remembered that he lived on the bottom floor of the complex.
" Shit. "

question: A planet rotates once every 1,000 years so that each side is either tundra or desert; the poles are also frozen wastes, but there is a small area of ever moving habitable land. Two nomadic tribes isolated on each side of the planet begin to find the 500 year old relics of the other.
answer:
The history of our people was first written on skins, with paint made of what was left after harvest. Nothing more was sacrificed however and our earliest history is often recorded solely in song. Just under 3 rotations ago on the Moon 1 RE our people decided that living in stagnation was no longer satisfactory and we began to keep records and The Order of Historians was born. For over 45,000 moons The Order has meticulously recorded every discovery, every success, every decision and every failure of our society in triplicate.
The three libraries travel by caravan separately such that the destruction of any one would not destroy our past. Each scroll is hundreds of meters long and contains over 100 moons of our history. It takes dozens of carriages to carry them all and several hundred to carry the members of the order and those that support them. The Academy of Science has been experimenting with a more compact method of storage, few of us understand it however and The Order has yet to trust it so the scrolls remain.
One rotation ago The Order enacted a plan to build three libraries with hopes that they could provide additional insurance against the loss of history. We will soon be upon the First Library built by the Order. Over the past moon the library has grown more and more visible and the Academy believes we will be able to safely journey to it in four unxtens.

question: " Lamb, tell me a story... ", said the Wolf.
answer:
“ Lamb, tell me a story… ” said the Wolf, with a smug voice and a smile on his face. “ ….Something sweet. ”
The Lamb trembled with fear. He had heard stories of the wolf all throughout his childhood, but never thought that there was any truth to them.
“ W-what would you like to hear? ” The Lamb finally asked.
“ You can decide that. ” The Wolf replied with an authoritative voice.

question: In the year 2300, the most commonly-consumed meat is human flesh. The majority of people are fine with this. Explain how the world got to this point, accepting cannibalism.
answer:
Prison overpopulation had been running out of control for years before the bovine flu epidemic. Millions of cows died in the span of a month, and all beef or dairy products were immediately recalled. They said it would be years before the industry recovered. Chicken and pork could only supply so much, and eventually people started going hungry.
Around the same time, a bill was quietly pushed through Congress that claimed to solve prison crowding and the food shortage at the same time. Officially, death row inmates or prisoners with life sentences would be allowed to donate their bodies to science. In reality, they were shipped to slaughterhouses and " processed". Over time it became less of a choice, and receiving a life sentence was no different from being given a death sentence.
Naturally the press eventually caught wind, and the initial reaction was predictably violent. Riots rocked the nation, and several cities enacted martial law. There were reports of live ammunition being used in Oakland, but nothing more than rumors ever surfaced. Over time the streets emptied, and people returned to their lives. Many rationalized the news, saying the murderers and rapists being harvested deserved it. Years later, outrage faded to quiet protest, and eventually acceptance. Companies avoided using the word " human" on their products, and it became easy to forget what we were eating. In the end, apathy won out over morality.

question: " So you went to the kitchen, made some toast, poured some coffee... and now there's an inter-dimensional portal?? "
answer:
At first, I thought it was just the garbage disposal acting up again.
I smacked the bottom of the sink with my mug, lightly, but the faint sound of whirring did not stop.
In fact, it only grew louder. Into an almost kind of growl that made me afraid it would wake Betty.
I bent down closer when the first glow appeared. What was that, I wondered. I squinted, thinking I might reconcile sight and sound.
" Hello? Hello?"
A shadow darted across the radius of the drain. My panicked hands dropped everything.
If I had known at the time what would happen, I would have grabbed my slice of toast from the bottom of the sink.
(Though, in my defense, I had little experience at the time with the inter-dimensional deification of baked goods.)
As it was, I swooped my snoring Betty up into my arms and over the sink. Startled, she farted her way more strongly than usual into consciousness.
I watched her watching for any sign, figuring her senses were sharper than mine.
Until an angry shout and a gray gloved hand reached up and dragged her down the drain. And I was now officially trapped in the morning that would never end.

question: Write a goodbye letter to the last year, explaining why you're leaving it for the next year.
answer:
Dear 2013,
One year ago, today, I sat down and made myself a promise that I would set out to transform myself into a new, better person. The person I had hoped I would become over the course of the year would be a complete stranger to the person making these goals. I would improve on my shortcomings and I would find strengths to conquer my weaknesses. The person that sat down to make this promise was someone who couldn ’ t be trusted, a person who didn ’ t deserve the friends he somehow managed to have. He was someone who saw his reflection and didn ’ t like what he was looking at. That is when he decided to make 2013 the year that he finally became the person he had always dreamed he could be.
As the pages on the calendar fell, so did those goals that he so eagerly set for himself. His optimism proved to be a false prophet. He betrayed himself again and again.
And that is why I must bid farewell to you, 2013. I can ’ t take another day of failure or another moment of letting myself down. In 2014, I must strive to be the man that I was supposed to become last year.

But I had never faced an enemy I did not know.
Humans, crooned the Queens. Kill them, shouted the Kings.
So we obeyed.

question: After the zombie apocalypse, a man prepares to do the most vital thing to fortify his house. Mow the lawn.
answer:
I didn't believe it at first, when the zombie apocalypse started. My dad had always been a bit obsessed though. When I moved out, he gave me a whole crate of supplies. Guns, knives, a machete, and enough food and bottled water to last a month. There were also a few packets of seeds from somewhere called Bloom & Doom Seed co., but I had no idea why they were in there. But when the apocalypse started, I grabbed that crate and got the he'll out of Dodge city. An hour later, I was pulling up to my childhood home on the edge of suburbia.
It was the first time I had been back to the house in a few years, and I was concerned by how run-down it looked. The lights were out, the grass was long, and there was no cars in the driveway or garage. Dad hadn't been here for a few months, at least. Even without him, this was probably one of the safest places on Earth. He had been crazy prepared.
I unlocked the door and quickly made my way to the basement. Anything and everything Dad had stockpiled would be there. I flicked the switch, casting a dim light over the large crates. All of them had a logo, but not one I expected to see.
Bloom & Doom Seed co.
I was confused. Dad was obsessed with surviving the apocalypse, why did he have nothing but plants? I grabbed a small booklet laying on one of the crates, hoping for an explanation. A few minutes later, I understood.
First, I had to mow the lawn. It wouldn't do to have my defensive lines blocked by the tall grass, after all.

question: A person manages to turn their life around just in time for an apocalyptic event.
answer:
I can not believe they did it.
They did it, they found a cure.
I held the piece of paper in my hand that had my name and the news on it.
*Because of your condition you are automatically enrolled in new treatment procedures, please contact the number provided for immediate care. *
My mom was still crying to my grandma on the phone. " My baby is going to be okay! Yes! He's going to be okay."
I smiled and turned to walk outside, the sun was out and the skies were blue, not a single cloud in the sky.
I get to live, I get to see fifty. I get to have kids, everything has changed.
I walked out to the sidewalk and look both ways down the empty street, then raised my face up to the sun feeling the heat on my skin and my head. I rubbed my bald head, feeling it.
I can grow hair again.
I fell backwards on the grass, smiling, laughing, moving my hands through it. Everything was different now! I get to live! Fuck! I get to have a girlfriend, I get to drive a car, I get to --
I paused as I felt the sun disappear, a great giant shadow enveloped me and the rest of the neighborhood. I looked up see a mammoth fireball moving across the blue sky, a heavy grey and black smoke streaked from it.
I heard my mom scream from behind me.
" David! Inside! Now!"

question: " Don't worry, your death will be as informative as possible. "
answer:
I held security on a berm above the high brown grass of the river bank, oriented out towards the nearby town, but there was no one outside. Others held their weapons pointed towards the other side of the river, to where the ones we hadn't killed escaped. My crusty staff sergeant asked if I wanted to come and see. I came off my position and walked down into the tall reeds and stared blankly at the 17ish looking, dirty brown Pakistani boys whose backs and skulls were split open from 30mm rounds. I took a moment to try and remember all the details, not just the way they looked, but what had brought them to this moment. We had shadowed danced all morning, not firing a shot, until finally, through maneuver, we had pinned them against the river, and called in the A-10's. I wanted to remember the little things in case I could capture any teachable moments. An emotionless voice, not my own, somewhere from inside my head addressed the bodies, " You are going to be used in an attention getter, or a powerpoint slide some day."
Nodding to Staff Sergeant, I climbed back up the steep, sandy berm to hold security. A sweet 19 year old kid from Minnesota came down later with a group of " quick" reaction forces, and loaded those two and the other bodies into bags. While the kid bagged them, I thought to myself, “ Isn ’ t that something ”. I was glad I hadn ’ t had to carry the thirty five pound radio jammer that day. It was bulky and heavy and we ended up staying outside the wire for almost twelve hours.

question: " I love you Ellie, " you whisper to your dead sister's photograph on the night stand. " I love you too, " She replies.
answer:
I look out over the bombed out valley and look at the crumpled picture in my hands. " I love you Ellie."
" I love you too," Ellie says as she sits down on the rock beside me.
" How are mum and dad holding up?" I ask as I take a swig from the half-empty canteen beside me and offer it to her; she politely declines, she never was one for drinking.
" They're doing ok, they miss you like hell and mum spends most of her time trying to watch over you; dad's trying to fill his days to avoid thinking about what happened."
" Yeah, yeah," I sigh, " I can imagine it's hard on him." I light a cigarette, again Ellie declines; it's good she hasn't picked up any of my habits.
Her eyes soften as she turns to me, I adjust the rifle hanging from my shoulder and an explosion rings somewhere out in the distance.
" But how are you holding up after everything that happened?"
" Eh, I'm holding up," I lie with a slight chuckle. She knows I'm lying, her eyes say it all. She knows how messed up I am, that I've been drinking to cope with the pain and taking night patrols to get out of the base and clear my head. " God knows how this war's going to end and God knows if I'll even see the end of it, but I just have to carry on as best I can." I shake my head and sigh before the radio cracks and I'm brought back to reality. Ellie vanishes, my flask runs dry and I'm reminded once again that I'm losing my damn mind.

question: (credit to /u/Arandmoor) I'm tired of fantasy where Elves are 'better than you ' just because they're elves. Give me some sword & sorcery, fantasy-style, where typical elder fantasy races learn why it's not wise to mess with 'mere ' humans.
answer:
" Why human?" Elder Sakhalev asked to the war council.
" Humans are weak, not physically strong like Orcs nor technologically advanced like the Dwarves, nor magically reinforced like the Goblins. Humans are essentially a low-hanging fruit ripe for picking." General Atgentes, the leader of Elven Incursion answered after sheathing her blade.
" You would be wise not to underestimate the humans. There are reasons why they stands as our equal in Five World Alliance." Murmurs could be heard from the war council.
" Three hundred years ago, maybe. Right now, humanity is just a barbarian race without distinct magical, physical nor technological advancements."
" Those in favor on invading humans?" Only Elder Sakhalev and two others didn't raise their hands.
It was carnage.
True, humanity has no giant cannons that made the Dwarves formidable, nor the magical fortification that renders the Goblins invulnerable, but their armies pushed us back regardless.
General Atgentes crossed her sword with a human soldier, magical explosion made the surrounding air heats beyond hospitable. And yet the human soldier recklessly slashed her armor, skillfully dodging the explosions while their mithrill swords shattered her armor pieces.
" Have you seen the power of humanity, Elven scum."
" Tch, mithrill, the metal of the legends. No wonder humanity could survive this long."
" You made a fundamental mistake there, miss General." The soldier shattered her blade " Us human survived not because our affinity to mithrill." before burying his own to her heart.
Her consciousness fading, General Atgentes vaguely heard the soldier speaking. " It was because our ability to unite the Five Worlds that we're able to wield mithrill in the first place."

answer:
" So I guess you want to me to explain those shoes and the katana before I explain why I speeding? That's stupid."
" Really, you find the shoes and katana more interesting? I recall speeding is against the law but shoes and katana aren't."
" Uhhuh."
" I'm glad you understand. So let me explain why I was speeding. I wasn't aware I was speeding. I was just rushing to work."
" No, why would I observe my speedometer."
" Why I don't look at my speedometer? Good question. I guess I was rushing for work."
" What work? I will explain."
" I am a priest."
" Priest of what religion? Oh, you probably never heard of it but let me tell you something. Our religion is all about enlightening people, young children in fact. At times, we target those who need enlightening. Particularly leaders of countries too. Particularly, people who don't live in Japan or Germany. We usually work together."
" Well, the shoes are just a gift from them after we enlightened them. I'll continue. We usually enlighten them by showing them an image of the true god and our tools. Usually we work together."
" How do I explain the katana. Well, our religion was first started in Japan. We were sent to various countries during World War 2 to educate as many people as we can. The katana is a tool of ours."
" Well, my target has probably boarded his flight already. But never mind, you seem to be a suitable candidate. I guess I'll just have to make do with you, my poor American. Goodbye."

question: From what two cops can hear in the next room, they believe there is going to be a possible drug deal. As they barge into the room, they discover something quite different.
answer:
Decorated officers, Trigg Freedomfries and Brick McNutjob burst into the cartel safe-house, their guns blazing in righteous fury.
" Not on my watch!" screamed Trigg, as he emptied one clip after another into the dirty, drug-dealing thugs.
" Brick Smash! ", bellowed officer McNutjob as he dropped his empty gun and began beating a particularly tiny drug-dealer to death with his baton.
When the screams finally stopped several minutes later, officer Freedomfries gently pulled his friend off of the dead toddler who's head he had smashed into a fine paste.
Trigg's steely eyes surveyed the scene, noting how odd it was that the cartel was using a family of four as a front for their operation... and did they really think a banner reading " Happy Birthday Katylin" and a " My Little Pony" themed birthday cake would fool the multi-billion-dollar intelligence machine of the DEA?
Just then dispatch crackled on Brick's radio. Brick listened intently, his face growing slack, a stream of drool dripping from his gaping mouth as he concentrated on the word-noises. " Word-noises hard", thought Brick, wishing the noises would stop so he could go back to bludgeoning the dead child at his feet.
Finally, after grappling with the word-noises for several minutes, Brick turned to Freedomfries and said, " Tiny woman in box on Brick's shoulder say this wrong house."
Trigg sighed heavily, " Damn. More victims of the drug-culture that's destroying our great nation." Officer Freedomfries lifted his gaze, eye's bright with freedom-tears, " But you won't be forgotten random citizens - you are heroes."
Brick stared silently at his partner for several seconds, " Brick want donuts."
Freedomfries looked over at his partner, " Yeah, you've earned'em buddy, let's get some donuts."

question: You're on a quest through the desert, but get bitten in the heel by a venomous snake. As the venom begins to take effect, you realize there is no chance of survival
answer:
Tell me how the girl fell through her skin.
Was there blood or fireworks inside her belly?
Did the fever pitch her right over the side of the cliff,
Or did she climb down gradually?
Sometimes we are snowflakes,
So different we just melt at human contact.
Such anger in the cold.
Such passion in the heat.
I know this. I have always known this.
I walked the grassy hills for hours,
Because I lost my sense of self.
Funny how in the last hours of existence,
when the mountains become faces gazing down,
the sky is hospice blue,
The white walls around my eyes closing in.
The wind withholding all but the pine,
of a well worn death.

question: " Just because you're holding a gun, doesn't mean you're in charge of the situation "
answer:
" Wave that thing all you like — you're finished here." Her voice, cold as winter wind, cut through me.
I adjusted my grip on the gun, my fingers slick with sweat. I had to shut her up or she would tear us apart. I could see the furtive glances at one another, the hushed whispers, the suspicious eyes cast my way, and I knew I didn't have any more time.
" You shut your mouth!" I barked, thrusting out my arm as though I were holding a lance or spear. " You don't know anything about us! I should -"
The wolf wearing a woman's skin took another casual step towards me. " Stop talking before you make things worse." I seethed at how she could stun a room into silence and take a man's words from him.
" I understand perfectly. You need to leave, John. Your time playing chief with these," she spared a disdainful look at the squalor around us, " ruffians is over."

question: Write a poem gracefully describing the symptoms of an illness / disease of your choice.
answer:
SUNSET
I'll chase away the suns incandescence till I finish with the consolation prize of vertigo
*I don't like the sun*
Breathe heavy, here's to me, celebrating another breath while so many others don't get to grow old,
We're all cats running out of our prescribed nine lives,
Light is my disguise for the darkness that cried wolf in front of an audience of assumptions left to writhe as rose vines performing lingchi on the naivety that preceded warning signs,
Only the owls can see the life that leaks from every itch because it's *their* talons hidden inside of you and I

The rays pierce sanguine skin promising warmth,
Yet as I bask under her sallow form all I feel is her icy gluttonous sardonic stare nurturing the fields of germinating despair,
So cold, so distant, malignant, inconsiderate, save me from her glare that left me impaired with a life already in disrepair,
I'm lost inside a road map full of dead ends and wrong turns, eyes fixated at the sun fixated on me fixated at myself
*I don't like the sun*

question: God has his workers create a prototype for a species called 'human '. Some of the decisions they took really baffle God. He calls in his minions to explain these decisions
answer:
" Yes, but no fur, Gabriel? Really?! We ALWAYS do fur! How on earth will the poor beasts stay warm?!" God's voice thundered around the palatial chamber in heaven, bouncing off it's cloud-constructed walls.
" Ah, but sire," the angel's voice quivered just a bit as he stood before the throne, " These being are exceptionally intelligent. They'll rapidly conceive the idea of using the pelts of other animals for warmth."
This gave God pause. It certainly was something new.
" Fair enough, fair enough," he finally responded. " But with that kind of intelligence, you run the very real risk of them figuring it out."
" Figuring what out, sire?"

question: Take any mundane task and turn it into an adventure.
answer:
It started out like any other day, but this day quickly turned dark. I knew what I needed to do. I took a deep breath, convincing myself that I had to do it - for my family. I grabbed the keys off the hook, and flung open the door. The bright sunlight glared off the white vehicle and nearly blinded me. I held my arm up to shield myself from the harsh rays, and stepped out into the constricting heat.
I finally made it to the vehicle and climbed inside, already parched. I wiped the sweat from my brow. I again had to convince myself that it had to be done; there was no one else. I glanced over my shoulder a couple of times to make sure there was no one nearby, then slowly started the trek down the driveway. Once to the street, the chaos ensued. Cars were flying by, left and right. I felt trapped, and I couldn't turn back now. I eased forward slowly and waited for my chance. There was a small gap and I took it. I slammed the accelerator to the floor and lurched out, taking the slim break in stride. I made it.
After arriving at my destination, the choices of where to stop were vast and nearly endless. I drove around in circles for quite some time, growing more and more tired as I went. I didn't know if I was going to make it. Then I spotted it. I made my way across the path and noticed someone else that was also noticing my spot. I sped up. I barely squeezed into the parking spot before the other car, missing the bumper by what seemed like mere inches. I had arrived.
Walstore, here I come. And I need butter!

question: A Man dies in a small town and is reanimated as a zombie. His soul, now a ghost, follows his old body around, preventing it from getting into too much trouble. The first human that the zombie bumps into is you.
answer:
Part 1
After the nuclear plant explosion, things were never the same in the neighboring town sitting 5 miles north. It has only been 6 months since the explosion, but already, people are dying. Many die without pain, but others die in agony. As the town mortician, it's my job to assist in the burials. I try to be careful with the handling of the bodies.
Before the nuclear plant explosion, (tragic accident I might add, killed about 100 plant workers instantly), I used hand sanitizer religiously but I never wore what I'm wearing now; a bio-hazard suit. I do not want to get contaminated by whatever is killing these people. Some say it's the radiation that's killing them, but others say it's the chemicals that oozed out into the air after the explosion. I'm not a scientist, I'm a mortician, so I have no idea what it could be.
Some of the bodies I've seen react in very strange ways. Most bodies will naturally twitch from time to time, but most of these bodies that I've handled, twitch a little too much. I'm not sure why, but we have to bury them as soon as we get them, so I haven't played much Dr. Frankenstein with them, yet. Bodies are coming in quick, and families don't have money to pay for a proper funeral. So as soon as I get them, I feed them to the earth. What can I say, I've been a bit desensitized. And today, I'm too tired to carry this last body to the cemetery. Not like it's going anywhere anything time soon!
Morning arrives. The mortician named Alex enters lab. He's unable to find the body he left on the table last night.

question: You have been shot through space in a cryogenic freeze. You finally unfreeze and find that you are a museum artifact on an alien planet.
answer:
" Sign up for intergalactic space travel, they all said. It'll be fun." I muttered quietly to myself. Damn, I should've used the restroom when I had the chance. Looks like I'll just have to hold it in.
I take one last look around before I close my eyes. I notice that everyone is in separate detachable pods. That seems a bit odd, but I guess that is just a fail safe feature, in case something happens to the main ship. I look down at the bottom of my pod and notice that its not properly attached. I start to panic, then complete darkness.
I wake up and instantly start to urinate, I couldn't hold it in. I let out a shutter, its freezing in here. My vision is blurred and foggy, I can faintly see figures slowly stepping away from me. I rub my eyes until I can see clearly. There is an oddly shaped ice sculpture with a hole in its chest lying on the floor in front of me. I notice that there is a shiny gold circlet around its head. I hop out of the pod, and stumble to the ground.
When I look up, I'm surrounded by these ice sculptures. They're making a bunch of weird sounds that are progressively getting louder. Their voices remind me of thunder. Not sure what to do, I grab the circlet and put it on. When I stand up with it, they all kneel. I smile and say " Let the fun begin."

question: A situation that seems absolutely horrible, until the last sentence.
answer:
The taste of death never leaves your tongue.
Smoke stacks billow at the edge of the horizon, the only remnants of civilization. I strain to see more, but the dust whipping into my eyes from this unrelenting wind is making it impossible. My skin feels cold as the blood drains from my arms, the first time it had felt cold in months, and the ground rushes to meet my face.
Breaths are coming shorter now. I'm relieved. The caustic air shreds my lungs with each breath.
I am one of the last, the few who survived the initial blasts. It is possible that with me, humanity dies. I don't know. I don't care.
The mutations had come on quick. They started several years ago, a horrible plague killing our babies within the first few months of their lives, their skin cracking and shedding black flakes, purple lips quivering as their eyes went cloudy. The great death, they called it. Black death was already taken.
Growing up, my parents had told me two things disproved God, evolution and suffering. I had witnessed both together, and it had only served to do the opposite. I had to believe in God. How could I hate him if I didn't?
Spontaneous generation had been a myth, but it had come. Darwin had theorized that the mutations that could not survive in the world died out, but he had underestimated the stubbornness of man.
My eyes close as I feel the cold touch of a mutant, no more than three years old. " For you, we moved mountains. What will you do?"
I feel a spasm, but I have one last task, one last gift to give the next iteration of our race. I die with a smile on my face.

question: Write a story where everything is spiders.
answer:
Like a dark, skittering laser beam, they came from space.
It's been nearly two months since Arachnid Rain struck a quiet forest in Manitoba. Witnesses have since been engulfed in the flood, but scientific estimates and aerial helicopter views describe the impact zone as a towering column, about ten meters wide. The tower, perfectly aligned vertically, pours down spiders like a faucet in slow motion.
Even the highest tree tops of the forest became completely obscured by the growing pile in a matter of hours. The pile expanded outward, engulfing nearby towns and cities, until it covered every inch of the whole province, with no signs of stopping. Citizens were informed to evacuate, but with no end in sight to the onslaught of bugs, people couldn't be sure how far away would be safe.
Astrophysicists, meteorologists, and biologists were all puzzled. They couldn't predict the AR event, nor have they been able to explain its origins since. It defied scientific understanding of planetary orbits, of space travel, and of life in space. The current leading theory supposes that a wormhole above the planet had opened up to unleash concentrated hell, a theory allegedly proposed by a scientist throwing their hands into the air in exasperation. It certainly matches visual descriptions; people describe the rain as an unseen leak in the sky raining down a single, black pillar.
Canada became forsaken grounds. Neighboring continental countries quickly formed impromptu shelters on floating barges, ready for the flood of spiders to reach them. Fearing the worst, some private and government entities in Eastern continents began similar projects.
No armed militia could fight it. No walls could contain it. No science could understand it. Slowly, the Earth became spiders.

question: A person is drinking whiskey out of a bucket at a barbeque while standing next to an uncomfortable looking priest.
answer:
The priest looked at him, wary of what to say. The priest knew all too well the consequences of what tonight ’ s activities might bring. Still, it was a man of leadership he was looking at; he needed to approach this carefully.
Finally, the priest spoke up. “ Excuse me? ” he said. “ Do you think that is wise? ”
“ Wise? ” the man asked, almost choking on his whiskey. “ Wisdom has nothing to do with this. This is a feast, and a man should be allowed to enjoy his victories any way he wants! ”
The man looked down into his bucket, scowled, and started opening another barrel of whiskey. The priest briefly stretched out his hand, but hesitated. In situations like these, he was powerless. Who would listen to him, a thin, ragged old man? Yet he had to try. He had to save their leader from himself. He needed them as much as they needed him.
The priest stood straight, eyes fixed on the drunk man. He took a step closer and silently uttered a few words, praying with all his might that everything would work out. The man, now with his head entirely inside the barrel, suddenly fell asleep. A tiny drop of sweat ran down the priest ’ s forehead as he let out a sigh.
“ I ’ m sorry, ” he said quietly. “ But there ’ s another raid tomorrow. Another dungeon we need to clear and another boss to kill. You need to lead us again. We can not do this without someone to protect us. ”
There was no response from the drunk man except for slow, heavy breathing.

question: " I just came here to talk. No violence this time. "
answer:
" You say that every time, Frank. And then you give in," the woman said with a proud smile.
Frank, his gruff, weathered face full of emotion, looked down at his beat up old boots. " I can't help what I am," said Frank.
" I know," said the woman, in a sultry, seductive voice. She ran her hands down the curves of her black dress. " Just like I can't help what I am."
Frank pulled the knife out from his belt and raised it over his head. " I'm s-s-sorry," he stuttered.
The woman pulled back her long, auburn hair and stepped forward towards him.
Frank stabbed the knife down into her. She smiled, and collapsed on the floor.
Frank took the knife out of her, left the money on the nightstand, and walked to the door. " See you next week," he said.
After the door closed, the woman got up, and looked at her freshly healed wound.
No, Frank couldn't help what he was. But now he could take out his rage on her, instead of on helpless humans.
And she couldn't help what she was. Which is why she took the money and then went to see her connection down at the blood bank.
After all, you couldn't help who you were, but you could choose what you did with it.

question: Death is not some all powerful being. Rather, she's a socially awkward outcast. Somehow, you've managed to befriend her and things have started getting weird...
answer:
A quiet series of knocks on the door drew my attention. I looked up from my laptop, my eyes barely over the top of the screen.
The door slowly cracked open, and I saw her eyes peek in and scan the room, resting them on me, then veering over to the table to my right.
She slowly pushed through the doorway and tiptoed across the carpet, trying not to make a sound. Her oddly forced gait and mistimed pauses to look about was more than enough for me to continue staring.
She walked over to the table, on which a cage sat atop, with some bedding and a water container within.
She opened the cage, scooped out one of my older hamsters, and turned around, slowly tiptoe-ing in the same manner she came in.
With the hamster in one hand and the doorknob in the other, she gazed about one last time. A smirk and a half enthusiastic wave later, she left, door partially shut.
I looked back at my laptop screen and continued to browse.

" It's Grim Reaper," I correct for the millionth time.
" Aw, still a sourpuss as usual," Boogeyman says.
" Not much excitement in my line of duty," I reply glumly.
" Yeah, sorry I forgot, man. My life is so much more exciting. I get to scare kids when they're bad and... scare kids and stuff,"
" How are we related again?" I ask.
" Ya know, you're mother's sister's husband's aunt's cousin's daughter's son is my father!" Roger explains.
" Hmm," I reply, thinking. " In that case, you aren't immortal then, right?"
" Well, sort of. I can't die of old age, but if someone kills me my cousin, Jason C. Boogeyman, takes over,"
Jason isn't too bad of a guy.
" Hey, Roger, do you want to come with me?" I ask.
" Sure, man, can you show me where you take dead guys?"
" That's exactly where I was thinking of going," I reply with a cackle.

question: Write a story about a world where scientists gain powers based on the area of science they master. Your name is Albert Einstein.
answer:
My name is Albert Einstein. I'm a physicist - a stunted one. I'm lower on the pecking order than even economists, and even *they* can move money around. Most people ignore me - luckily, maybe. I don't know how long I would have survived at the top - star scientists lead a lonely life, always watching their back - and at least being a pariah gives me silence.
I have been working on my theory for the last two years, and I'm still not sure of it. I've been staring at that E=mc^2 for the last hour, but the math seems sound.
I did it. I did it, I did it, I did it!
Now I can see how it works. How everything works.
Energy equals to mass per speed of light squared...
I extend a finger, sparks playing over it. There is a flash, and a boom, as a cubic centimeter of air is suddenly turned into energy. I'm flung to the wall by the explosion, but time slows down to a crawl. I float down to the ground, gravity seemingly unaffected.
People come running though the door. " Albert, are you ok?" " What the hell happened here?!"
I get up, and look around in the destroyed lab. I smile widely. I must look silly, smiling with my hair raised on my head, but I don't care.
I finally got my powers.

question: You die and enter the afterlife... except its not what your religion described. In fact, its not what any religion described.
answer:
Endless space. Endless matter. Endless time.
Dying wasn't so bad in the end. I remember it clearly... I was always warned about office chairs. A blood clot took me quickly and relatively painlessly, I just passed out there and woke up here.
At first it was nothing, just a grey oppressive fog. Like someone had turned the rendering distance way down on reality. But I wanted a flashlight, and one manifested. That was the manner of interfacing with this space. Will it, and so it shall be. It was paradise. I actually reached heaven, and had total freedom. Total dominion. Total control.
I crafted beautiful landscapes, and wondrous industry. I didn't even need to understand the technology, if I willed a machine, one appeared that did what I required. All the video games and entertainment I could ever want.
I... I I I I. Even reading my own words I see the traces of the awful truth. Everything is " I". Everything is of myself. No other life. Perfect agency means perfect isolation.
I can only hope this isn't the end. Perhaps this is some final fantasy the brain spits out to try and prolong it's consciousness. Maybe my years of play are really just seconds of dying.
I can't kill myself here, maybe that's my own brains defense against finally letting go. If I try and harm myself everything just flashes white then reasserts itself.
Or maybe this is the afterlife, and other people are just outside the barriers of my creations, waiting to be discovered.
I don't want to be alone.

question: Two people are in a public place, one has had the best news of their life, the other has had the worst news of their life. Unbeknownst to them, they share the exact same news.
answer:
It's what I assume is a busy night at one of the larger casinos. Technically, I'm here to make money counting cards, but as my traveling companion and fellow successful gambler reminds me, " it's Vegas, man!"
So I leave the blackjack table, fix my makeup, and spritz on some perfume, becoming the very picture of somebody you'd like to buy a drink for. (What can I say? Alcohol is expensive.)
A couple hours and several drinks later, I'm dancing, and an enthusiastic woman with a Midwestern accent knocks me to the ground. " Oh, I'm so sorry, honey," she slurs, clearly wasted. " I didn't mean to run into you like that." " Are you all right?" I reply dubiously.
Her response is loud, even compared to the boom of the bass. " I am DOING GREAT," she responds operatically, " BECAUSE I FINALLY GOT A DIVORCE!" She rumbas, or twerks, or *something*, off to knock over another innocent bystander, and I lose sight of her.
Later, I sit at the bar, smoothing disheveled hair and hoping I don't smell like the sweat of strangers. Jack made a few thousand tonight, but I'm not ready to sleep yet, so I debate ordering another drink when a man with a gray suit and dark circles under his eyes does so for me.
He doesn't initiate conversation, just stares ahead, so I politely ask " What brings you to Vegas, then?" He replies " I'm here to get drunk" flatly, with the intonation of a man on death row. " I'm sorry." " Don't feel sorry for me, sweetheart. It was my own damn fault... wife left me. Thought she was the one. Apparently not."

question: Where were you the day the last elephant died?
answer:
On the day the last elephant died
I stood stock-still in the short grass, green around my feet,
Watching the event as it happened. It was a pity
But crime is crime, and when the last elephant kills
One of ten billion men, all the souls in the world
Can't decry what it is - a murderer clad in grey baggy skin.
People sometimes call the human tendency to give
Greater value to life than the cold equations suggest
Somehow correct, not an error. I dispute this, I
Who has so little of life, would say -
What's the life of one of ten billion men,
One of yours, one of the ones who kill without malicious intent,
Next to mine? Mine, which burns solitary on this green grass?
In unique limitation, I became valuable. But I am not immortal, and not, by the spoken courts amoral.
Not at all.

question: In humanity's spacefaring future, we discover that our evolutionary path is unique. We have many qualities that, while trivial or mundane to us, horrify the other sentient species.
answer:
" Sir, we've got a problem. Specimen 82 has started the reaction again."
At this point it was almost instinct to process what I'd heard. I had anticipated this from the first day we picked up this creature. I pressed the emergency button I insisted be made for this cell.
I'd had my hand on the button this entire flight so I was prepared. I'd never been in such a volatile situation as this. We knew what they did from the get go but still head office insitined we take a specimen. I get paid well for what I do, but this is above and beyond.
Instantly the specimin and the threat became subdued.
" Medic! Get the specimin into the chamber"
The effort keeping these things alive better be worth it...
Of course it would be alright, once we established the atmosphere in their chamber again. They are pretty resiliant, and this type of emergency hasnt been the first time with them.
We never should have taken these creatures on board. Seriously? what kind of species can survive on oxygen yet still start a fire and cook their food?

question: Monsanto is shut down and all GMO products are banned all across the US. What are the ramifications and/or improvements?
answer:
Thousands of dogs are raided from shelters in the US to be euthanized and have their insulin harvested due to the banning of GMO products used to make insulin now for millions worldwide. Beef and pork prices plummet as lots are forced to sell millions of heads of cattle due to inadequate feed supplies. Insecticide for corn (granular and spray) triples in price and refuge bags of conventional non BT corn quadruple in price.
Argentina and Brazil farmers make a killing creating non GMO
seed stock.
Wal Mart shelves become well stocked with all purpose grass killers that cost pennies per gallon.

answer: Karen always loved snow. She couldn't get enough of the stuff. Maybe that was why she decided to die when she did. I'm sorry, I shouldn't say die. That's a harsh word. What's better? Passed? There's that word again. Died. An angry, bitter word. Seems like it's full of spite. And yet, it seems like it fits. She didn't pass. She died in pain. She died in her favorite chair, while her internal organs shut down. Her last thoughts weren't of snow, but of suffering. Regardless, she was free now. Free from pain, free from scars. So, while her last thoughts were of suffering, I wanted my last thoughts of her to be what she cherished most: atmospheric water vapor frozen into ice crystals and falling in light white flakes or lying on the ground as a white layer. Or rather, snow. So, after the roads were clear, I called the mortuary, and told them where I wanted her buried. The beautiful, pristine white snow that Karen loved so much was blemished and destroyed by the mortuary-branded hearse. Maybe it was fitting. I don't know. All I know is she's gone and I'm still here. I wonder if it snows in Tahiti.

question: The zombie apocalypse finally happens! However, it only lasts about a month before the corpses are too rotted to move
answer: When it started, we didn't flee like you'd think, we didn't panic, we didn't leave people behind. I guess all of those zombie apocalypse movies helped our judgement. We formed walls, blocked off the zombies. After the initial outbreak, getting infected was rare. We developed specific quarantines, with daily checks for the virus on every individual in every country. We were organized, and we were winning. We got cocky, started experimenting on the zombies. Nobody knows exactly how it started, maybe someone who didn't want to die somehow evaded the medical checks, maybe some crazy bastard just got himself infected, but when the virus finally broke loose, it spread fast. Half of the country in 2 days. All of it in 2 weeks. All of the world in a month. Then, as quick as it happened, it stopped. A few days after the fall of Sweden, the last real government, the zombies stopped, their corpses rotted so much that they couldnt use their muscles, meaning no biting scratching, or movement. They were just corpses. Me and Adam are all that is left of California, everyday, we wade through the corpses, looking for others, we don't know what it is like elsewhere, the Internet fell with Sweden. The cell towers still work though, so that is where we are heading next, hopefully we can find others. But for now we will just wade, through corpses, water, and blood, watching, and waiting for a sign of life. I've been thinking of changing my name. I don't want to be reminded of my old life. What do you think of Eve?

question: Start your story with " After eons spent watching humans, I already knew that the most exhilarating and terrifying moment of my tenure would be when one started watching back. "
answer:
After eons spent watching humans, I already knew that the most exhilarating and terrifying moment of my tenure would be when one started watching back. It surprised me how quickly it happened, though. They were smarter, it seemed, than I had intended them to be. They had only just begun to truly wonder about my nature, their nature, when one of them decided I wasn't worth the trouble.
He was called Epicurus. He wasn't quite the first, but his words, his questions, stuck most clearly in my mind. He and his kind were what brought to mind those words: exhilarating and terrifying. Exhilarating, because now, I might have someone to talk to, someone to offer true feedback in regards to my project. Terrifying, because the someone who would offer that feedback must first see how poorly I had fared in the meantime.
Humility is a difficult thing. Almost as difficult as Creation.

question: Write about a typical match of Super Smash Bros. through the perspective of any of the characters.
answer:
It... it was insane. Out of all the things I've ever faced, this was by far the most terrifying. There was this guy who could literally punch you so hard his fist could catch on fire. There was a boy who had tamed a dragon to fight me. There were people sized animals with laser guns. There were two people who could just conjure ice. I didn't even know you could sign up as a team. Hell, I even met an angel.
But that's not even the worst part. Death wasn't the end. Each time I died I was just transported a couple of feet above the arena and dropped back down. But the pain never ended. After a series of being beat to death over and over, we were just sent out to fight again.
Even scarier than that, is how well people took it. There was this guy, dressed in medieval chainmail and green rags, armed with nothing more than a sword and shield. He went out there, against overwhelming odds, and even won sometimes. Against the magic animals. Against the monstrous pink blob. Against all the superior technology and magic. He went out there and he fought.
I guess he inspired me and I fought for a bit. Hell, I even enjoyed myself some. Met new people, made some friends and some foes.
So, I guess it wasn't too bad. I even learned the answer to a question I was asked long ago. Love *can* blossom on the battlefield. My only regret is not getting that chick in the power armor's number.

question: A Good News/Bad News Scenario where " Everything you know is wrong " is the Good News.
answer:
The world was bleak. Always gloomy. He was constantly on the move. Sometimes a feeling of unease would creep over him. He knew something was misplaced, there was something he was forgetting. But was it worth finding out? Perhaps it was just another dark secret better left unremembered and unspoken.
But still, on dark days he would look up and half-think he heard a voice. It was crazy, just the clouds and sunrays filtering in through the smog. But still he wondered.
He'd walk through a park, and look around a tree expecting something there. But what? What was he waiting for? There was never anyone there. There was never much anyone about. Just figures walking quickly by.
He never quite seemed to know what he was doing here. He had no dreams or aspirations. Everyone seemed in a hurry, but where were they going? He never could quite remember his purpose.
He woke up. His ceiling looked a lighter shade of grey today. In fact, his window was in a different place. His whole room had shifted, morphed. It was no longer the room he had fallen asleep in. And there was someone sitting in a chair. The man was in his early twenties and drowsing.
A pillow was thrown in that general direction.
" Hmphh, wha-?" He came awake. " Oh -- oh my God, Tom, you're awake?" His brown eyes burst into tears as he jumped from his chair. " I've -- I've hoped for so long, and waited, and --" He couldn't help himself from striding over and reaching out. " When we found out you had been in the car wreck -- the coma --" The strange man from the chair gripped hands with the now Tom. " Mom and Dad will be so happy!"

question: Write a fable with a terrible moral of the story.
answer:
A fox was making his way through the winter wood when he saw a curious thing. Children had been playing behind and left an army of grotesque snowmen. One sprouted five arms from its body, another had more eyes than a spider on its head, still another had two heads altogether. The fox sniffed and thought deprecating thoughts about the youth of today.
Suddenly the icy monsters came to life! They chased the fox through the wood, lurching through the snow. No matter where he hid, the abominable snowmen sniffed him out with carrot noses. Their coal eyes saw through the deepest camouflage and their wooden arms pulled apart the thickest brush.
Panting with exhaustion, the fox reached the bank of a half-frozen river. He was trapped! The snow monsters trundled towards him, arms outstretched. With no other choice, the fox dove into the icy river and swam through the cold. He reached the other side and shook the water from his coat.
The monstrosities hesitated for a moment on the other bank, then charged into the icy water. Almost immediately they fell apart - carrots and coal and limbs all floating off while snow bodies dissolved in the current.
The fox shook his coat again, sneezed, and carefully pronounced, " Snow goons are bad news."

question: Write about the exact moment a character betrays their best friend because they must.
answer:
The bridge is filthy. Clouds billow in the background but there's no breeze, just the smell of gasoline and tobacco. Pipes litter the area, and all the while there's the incessant racket of the chainsaws. His hands sweat. The sun is in his eyes.
Any false step at this point is certain doom. He pulls down his hat, adjusts his grip, and squeezes his legs; the steed obeys. Go on, just a little further now.
He's almost there. The end is in sight, but the divide is too large. He holds his breath without realizing while he assesses the situation. No choice but to try. Going back is not an option.
There he waits, mounted, atop a narrow spot of land. The bridge is behind him now, but the divide isn't getting any smaller. Time is running out. As any hope of a happy ending quickly fades, he realizes what must be done.
He swallows hard and spurs the beast. Faster now, at a gallop. The pit is rapidly approaching, and then it's time. They're airborne. Just when it looks like the void has been crossed, he does it.
He pulls the reigns, choking the only one that ever loved him. As they fall into the abyss the creature looks up to him, black eyes shining. In a weak voice, it says the one thing he's never forgotten.
" Go then, there are other worlds than these."
He plants his foot firmly in its back. There isn't much pain, not now, but the betrayal is worse than any knife. He gives one last look, then jumps. The beast looks on as he clambers up the far side.
He made it, but he'll never forget those pleading eyes.

question: You are the omniscient narrator of an antagonist who is starting to get the sense that you're watching them.
answer:
Jake watched the brothers in another one of their childhood escapades. He had seen them grow up. He loved them with all of his heart. He couldn't bear to let them live to see the horrible future that awaited them.
" Hey Dad!" said Timmy, or Timothy as he preferred to be called now that he was five. " Want to play ball?"
" I would love to," Jake replied, a tiny tear dripping from his eye. He knew what was going to happen in the next fifteen minutes. The world was going to end. He had ensured that. Slowly, Jake got to his feet and puttered down to his children's playroom, a gun hidden in his left hand.
Charles, his other child looked at his Dad. He was always the more prescient one. " Hey Dad," Charles said. His sky gray eyes gazed soulfully at his father's shaking hands. The two brothers always had a knack of anticipating and preparing for the future
Jake could hear the hydrogen bombs whistling in the wind. The sound of imminent and complete destruction sang its siren song in his ears. Too bad his children seemed unable to hear it.
" Charles, Timothy. Come here." Jake said, his voice wavered with doubt and concern. " I need to tell you guys a story."
The two brothers waddled towards their grey haired father who enveloped the two within his arms.
" There has been someone watching us." Jake said.
" Someone up there knows who we are. He knows our story. He knows why Stephen had to go away." Jake continued.
" I figured out how to stop him."
Then, Jake looked away from his children. His voice dropped into a mutter.
" Did you think I forgot about you?"

question: Write about a relationship that spans the length of a lifetime.
answer:
There is a picture of the two of us as babies sitting in the same seersucker jumpsuits our grandmother made for us. We used to be so small.
When we were both ten we would play around the house all day pretending to be some mythical hero or other. We used to be so happy.
In middle school we liked the same girl and would fight over who got to sit next to her on the bus. We used to care so much about things like that.
In high school we joined the football team so we could be cool, but we lost every game we played in. We used to think that mattered.
At eighteen we enlisted in the Army and went off to basic training, knowing we would not see each other again for some time. We used to be inseparable.
In 2005 we deployed to Iraq after working to be stationed in the same place. We used to want to be heroes.
On Thursday, 22 September 2005 he took a 7.62 mm round from an AK-47 through his eye. I used to have a brother.

question: You are able to experience the next day in advance when you go to sleep.
answer:
*Beep! beep! beep... *
I stretch out my hand, trying to locate my alarm clock and it's tiny'off' button.
Silence fills the morning, and for a moment I am relaxed in the soft light and the warmth of my covers.
Shit. Is it today? Is it really today? Again??
Sighing, I sit up in bed and rub my face with my hands. This whole'living the day twice' thing is getting really old. I mean, why should I even bother getting up and going about my day when I already know exactly what is going to happen?
Do I even have a choice?
I drag myself out of bed and into my morning routine.
Yep, stubbed my toe on the way to the bathroom. Oh look, there's no milk left. What's that? There's going to be an accident on the way to work? Of course there is, I've already dealt with this.
It's not all bad though. Today a stranger is going to pay for my coffee, I'm going to have an ok day at work and a really great dinner with my best friend. There'll be a fantastic sunset too, I'll marvel in its colours on my run this evening.
It's just that nothing surprises me anymore. Nothing excites me or moves me. How could it? I've already lived this day as I slept, and tonight I'll do the same with tomorrow, and tomorrow night the next day.. Always repeating, always prepared.
I'm not sure how I'm going to feel when my special " gift" prepares me for my final day on this earth.
To be honest, it might be a relief.

question: ... because when you're at the bottom, you'll follow anyone who makes you feel less of a failure...
answer:
That feeling when you've hit the bottom of the sea bed and all that's inside your head is the weight of your empty mind, full of what seems like nothing, but weighs more than is bearable. Sinking down, down, down, thinking that it can't get any worse but it will and it does.
You've been there for so long that it's become dull; the water around you has grown cold and cloudy. Your rock face has adapted a thick skin to keep out the unknown that is happiness. Until there's one person...
That one person that seems to break through the skin you thought was thick; they pick you up out of the polluted water and give you a breath of fresh air. You're more than willing to let them help you and you hold onto them like you once held onto your happiness, but stronger than ever. Terrified. Terrified to lose what seems like the only soul kind enough to notice you...
There it is. You feel it again, a sense of belonging, but the worry of losing them taunts you endlessly. Maybe you will lose them, and take the plunge into the depths of depression once again, but for now you hold on, waiting for the inevitable end...

question: Your coworker that sits next to you has been coming into work with horrible BO since you started working here a year ago. You have to do something
answer:
Roger Ho was not someone you would suspect of alternative cleansing means. He always wore nice slacks, a brown shirt, and decent shoes. He got his hair cut every two weeks and his teeth shown like a beacon of hope.
But he smelled. If Moses came down from the mountain with two giant laxatives, let the people of Israel devour them, then build an idol of shit -- that would be Roger.
If the moon was made of cheese and had been rotting in the sun for a million years. If the waves were powered by Aquaman's intestinal issues...
Well, that would be Roger.
When he lifted his arms, it was like a hot humid summer.
We had been trying to tell him for months. We bought him'nice' presents, baskets filled with bathing items. He said he gave them to his girlfriend.
How did he have a girlfriend?
Roger seemed to go through women quickly. He must have never hugged a lady until the third date, when they always seemed to go blind with pain and run into traffic. Or just leave.
And Roger never seemed to know why.
It wasn't like we could tell him! No, it would be harsh, rude --
" Duuuude! You smell like a congealed fart. You need to put on some deoderant, Roger, you have nasty B.O."
I looked up in shock. Amanda, the new girl, the pretty little blonde with a fetish for earrings?
She was waving her hand infront of her nose and pointing at him.
Roger looked horrified.
" I couldn't tell... I don't... I can't smell."
" Well, you stink."

question: The guard looked at me, then down at his gun, and back at me.
answer:
The guard looked at me with a pained expression, tears visibly flowing from his eyes. His breathing became quick and labored; his more than obvious gut jiggled back and forth with each breath. He looked to the gun in his hands and back at me in disbelief. I began to wonder, " What is he crying for? What happened? I know I heard a gunshot. Was it him or the robbers?"
I looked around the lobby of the bank and saw none of the masked robbers. " The fat fuck missed, didn't he?... why is everyone crowding around me?"
Then I looked down and saw the blood. At first I wondered where it was all coming from and then it hit me. A sharp biting pain that turned into a blood-curdling scream from my own lungs, only to be interrupted by the guard who had shot me. " SOMEONE CALL 911, OH GOD, OH GOD, I'M SO SORRY. STAY WITH ME. PLEASE GOD NO."
All the lights around me slowly began to dim and shake as if it were all just a mirage. Then there was only darkness and an eerie perfect silence.

answer: Any good helper is going to need you more than you need them. You want to make them feel powerful, like they can get what they want from you. Always though, leave them wanting more. Basically if you sit and stay for at least 3-5 seconds when they ask, you're pretty much guaranteed a treat. None of that mutt crap, real sit and stay. No wiggling, or wagging the tail. These days, I get pet for 45 minutes at a time, all because I learned to bate them in with " sit" and " stay". They can't get enough of it! Sometimes I bring the ball back for them after they throw it, that makes the helpers feel special. Kind of like I need them, but sometimes I keep it to show them they really need me, I call it playing hard to get. If your helpers bring friends over, get really friendly with them, it will make your helpers jealous and not only will you be pet by the visitors, but also rewarded. Basically its about training, give them what they like at the right time, and they'll learn to know their place.

question: When you die, you play a game of rock, paper, scissors with death. The reward is being able to relive the last day of your life with knowledge of your demise. You win.
answer:
As Death lays out the rules, I sigh. Of all the games...
Honestly, I'm just easily distracted. I get caught up in the preparation only to realise that I haven't decided what to do. Hence why I always end up choosing rock. I wonder absently if Death has seen me play before. Is he like an omnipotent God, aware of my complete inability to play this game well?
I pause to think as Death continues his spiel about'terms and conditions'. Honestly, nobody reads those while they're alive, does he really think I'm going to take notes now?
He holds out a thin, pale hand, clenched into a fist. I do the same, my fist looking a lot less imposing. We bring them up in sync as Death drawls out the three words.
" Rock, paper, scissors!"
My fingers spring to life (ironic, huh?) as he says the final word and as I look at my hand, I am almost shocked to see two digits extending from my fist.
What surprises me most, however, is that Death's hand lies flat. I did it. I won.
A bubble of fear rises in my throat and I run my hands through my hair as I look to Death.
" But I don't want to go back," I whisper. " Today was the worst day of my life."
There is a pause, then Death reaches up and lowers his dark hood. A smug smile spreads across his face.
" I know."

question: You have just completed your Death Ray. It destroys hopes, dreams, and aspirations.
answer:
Always, everybody else just seemed to happy. They always had something to do, something on their mind. They ran around, completing their goals, petty hopes and dreams that meant nothing in the end. Then they would smile, and other would smile and they would hug and kiss... or whatever shit it was they always did. They had this weird thing, this force driving them forwards, to do new things, and improve old things, to learn, to create, to master things more pointless than existence itself.
They always asked me, " What are your goals?", " What do you want to be when you grow up? ", " What is your favourite [ insert whatever here ]". They thought I cared, I did not care. I had no hopes, no dreams, no aspirations.
So I thought, why not show them the truth, why not show them the their weakness. They needed to learn.
& nbsp;
I went on existing, sucking in knowledge, taking their thoughts and ideas from them. I made sketches, I worked on concepts. eventually I made a prototype, then another. Eventually it worked. I had completed my " death ray", I had created the death of all hopes, dreams, and aspirations. They would suffer, they would learn my apathy, the world would take the grey hue I always saw it with.
I felt... success. I felt accomplishment. It felt wonderful, it felt awful. I had worked so hard to destroy everybody else, and in doing so, I had become one of them.
I guess I am worthless at everything, I'm not even able to keep the feeling of worthlessness going when I need it most. Why did I even try, I can never things well.

question: Humans are the only sentient species in the known Galaxy that " die " in any meaningful way. An alien species wants to understand our secret.
answer:
" Sir you need to see this." Keon said, afraid that he would not be believed.
" What is it?" replied his captain, Mal.
" Something has happened to the prisoner we took. I've never seen anything like it."
Mal looked up from his desk for the first time. question: None of the angels knew the true purpose of their halos. Yours just broke.
answer:
It happened so fast that it felt like time had come to almost a complete halt. I fell.
The crack it made was the equivalent of a Native American stepping on an unexpected branch during a hunt. It echoed through heaven as I returned. No one even seemed to notice. My wings blackened and turned into dead weight. As I plummeted, the laws of nature took effect. My wings turned to ash. The halo once above my head burned to nothingness.
There was one thought running through my head " What did I do wrong?!"
Then I landed. Softly. I thought I would die upon impact. But I didn't. I didn't know where I was. It wasn't anywhere on earth that I had visited before. A low, deep, growl called out to me.
" Welcome home, Lucifer."

question: They opened his veins, and sand poured forth.
answer:
They cut open his veins and the sand poured forth. The wraith shrieked and flailed, smashing its limbs against those who attempted to restrain it. Contorting its body and becoming formless, it escaped its shackles and bounded forward, a vision of fury. The blinding rage of the sand demon would not let itself by held down by mere mortals. The men swung their swords at it in futility, slicing through the pouring sand, then being asphyxiated by the vomit of the dunes. As many men as could beat a hasty retreat across the makeshift moat they had constructed. Sand could not cross water, without losing its form and separating.
The torches lit their gloomy faces and they glared at the monster, contemplating their next course of action.
Their newest recruit volunteered a solution: fire. Not just any fire, but an explosion. They quickly wrapped whatever gunpowder they had in their possession with a cloak, made a makeshift fuse and flung it across the water. The explosion knocked them off their feet. When the dust cleared, the oppressive silence told them one thing: tonight's ordeal might be complete, but more would come.

question: Describe the most boring thing you can imagine in the most interesting way possible
answer:
This was John's fourth detention this week.
" I will adhere to the code of conduct. I will adhere to the code of conduct. I will adhere to the code of conduct. I will adh..."
John was 30 minutes away. John 30 minutes from being excused, and allowed to go home for the day.
But he didn't mind.
He wasn't anxious to be anywhere. Despite being spoken ad nauseam, " I will adhere to the code of conduct. I will adhere to the code of conduct." had perplexed John in unforeseen ways.
It was semantic satiation at work.
The words were blending for John. Twisting, until they had lost all meaning, the physical packaging of ideas we coin'words' had unraveled in John's head. He was pondering far beyond his fellow recidivists. Firing neurons repeatedly in the same sections of his brain had led to a loss of sensation derived upon speaking the very words. It had become white noise. To some, boring and unworthy of further scrutiny, to John, an arousing notion.
The bell rang. They stopped speaking, and left. John left perplexed, but nonetheless had experienced a phenomena evidencing boredom's psychological effects, and the reality of its toll on the human psyche.

question: Fast food franchises have become the dominant religions. You meet some unsavoury acolytes of the Burger King whilst on a pilgrimage to Kentucky.
answer:
The acolytes stood in a line, twelve members strong, preventing passage along the road.
" Abandon the path upon which you stand, vermin! ", I bellowed.
The largest of the acolytes, and presumably the most senior amongst them from the number of holy stains on his garb, stepped forth from the line. The thin plastic mask he had adorned, portraying the heretical visage of The King, betrayed no emotion or intention.
I redoubled my efforts: " You have no authority under your sect to interrupt a pilgrimage! Stand aside!"
The leader unleashed a guffaw appropriately proportionate to his belly;
" The light of The King knows no bounds! We will stand wherever his grease can touch!"
He took another step closer.
" The King has also showed us the path to salvation! In his texts, in the signs and dreams he gave unto us!"
Another step.
" The One, True Burger is all that can save humanity from wretched sin! Those who will not abandon the inferiority of the Fried Chic-"
The head of my Bucket Mace^TM collided with the mask, scratching at the cheap paint. Before he had a chance to recoil I swung it round again, the bone spikes piercing plastic and skin. In a fury I roared:
" Come and face me you heathens! All those who would deny the power of KFC would dare to test it!"
As the grunts drew weapons, moving to surround me, I felt a warmth fall upon me. I raised my eyes to the clouds, and saw a shape in the clouds.
The face of the Colonel. He smiled down on me.
Today was a good day.

question: Hi, Bye. Thats how simple it used to be..
answer:
Hi, Bye. That's how simple it used to be.
Before things got more complicated and two words turned into three.
Before I turned to you one day and asked you " what of us?"
And you retorted that I perhaps should ride the special bus.
Long before the wine, the drugs, the sex that made us cry
The tears of joy now disappeared and replaced by smiles wry.
That's how simple it used to be.
" What of children?" I ask and you reply without a thought
" Our lives are far too fun to live them with tensions drawn so taught"
So compromise did I on this, and so you did with that,
Calamities did pass us by, and lies were told too fat.
Now across from me you sit, your tears can not hold back,
The last half truth I told to you just broke the camel's back.
As we gaze, and cry, and laugh, and frown you stop and muse to me:
" Hi, Bye, do you remember how simple it used to be?"
And I do remember, very well.

" You don't understand my plans. I will change the way the world turns, forever," the Growler spoke out loud as darkness covered the lands.
