question: You are having dinner with your family, when someone knocks on the door.
answer:
You approach the door. Confused at the hour at which the knock has come, not having expected company. Upon opening the door you are greeted by the sly grin of the pizza delivery man, barely recognizable in the dim luminescence of the porch light. Befuddled, not remembering placing an order for pizza, he speaks, " did somebody order a....pizza."
Boom! In one fluid motion, he rips off his clothes and techno music starts playing in the background. Unh tss unh tss unh tss!
He starts dancing, gyrating his hips. Horrified, you turn around to see your toddler staring in the direction of the front door seemingly entranced by the dancing. The man steps further into the light, getting ever closer to the threshold of the door. The unseen force of recognition slaps you upside the head. With anger and disgust in your voice you scream at the man, " Uncle Bernie! Lay off the sauce!" Slam!

question: Write about a tense political situation then defuse it with a thumb war.
answer:
It was the year 2052.
" Give Crimea!"
" No, you!"
" I want Crimea!"
The situation had gotten worse over the years. Crimea was famous for being the most contested place on Earth. I lived there. Every day I would hear explosions on my way to school. I would hear explosions while I was sleeping, I would hear guns firing, I would hear the news about what was happening on our little peninsula... every time I tried to watch cartoons on TV.
Three years later... there was a ceasefire. In the treaty, the leaders of Ukraine, the Crimean Nationalist party, and the Russian Federation were to have a three-way thumb war to see who would occupy Crimea for the next 100 years.
My family's side lost.

question: You win every game you've ever played, but for some reason you refuse to play the only game that matters.
answer:
Tuesday, 13th May, 2015
Dear Diary,
'The Game Master', is this week's name. I think I've made more money from publicity than I have from any game show I've ever been on. Even when the head corporations of television battled it out with one another to get me to sign their latest idea, it hadn't even come close to the amount earned from... well... *doing nothing*.
I don't know why, I don't know how. What I do know is that to the public, I have two sides, that battle one another in their opposite opinion, like a political party trying to knock the other side out of their morals and beliefs. My name is irrelevant, the person I am is most certainly irrelevant, but I can't really expect anything more.
*" Life is game" *, my late mother told me. The only woman I knew that understood me for who I was and that meant, the only person who knew I could never stop doing what I'm doing, even if I tried. She'd say I've got myself in to this mess and there's no way of turning back the clock, but, before I even realised that everything I won was something more than just'luck', it was already too late.
I suppose all I can do is play this out. Ha... The irony...'playing' this out just adds insult to injury, really, doesn't it? When I first realised what I could do, it was great, but looking back, I should have just gambled with a high prize scratch card, got rich, and lived my life in a place where my first name wasn't Cheater and my second name wasn't Lucky.
I know which one I'd prefer... But which one I deserve? I can't admit. Until tomorrow, Diary.

" But is it *conscious*?"
" We have no way of knowing. For its sake, I hope it is not."

answer:
Two years... Two years of living hell, no companionship except for the... creatures that came alive at night. Two years of scavenging food and water from the ruins of New York. After the first year I'd given up on finding another human, and moved out from my hidey-hole in the city, found a defendable house in the suburbs. The American Dream, revised for the busy apocalypse-survivor.

I peer through the window and see it, see that it's real. It's been modified with mounted guns and armour and treads, but it's still a goddamn ice cream truck.
I see the silhouette of the driver through the tinted window. I consider running out, yelling for him to stop, but I know better. My mother taught me when I was a kid that they only play the music when they've run out.

answer: The crackling noise behind me is the only warning I get. I drop to the ground just in time to avoid the beam of raw energy passing overhead. I have had enough experience to know just how lethal that beam, composed of lightning, steam, and death itself, is. I also know there is no chance for diplomacy. That monster following me is the embodiment of pure chaos and destruction. Nothing can curb it's destructive tendencies, no reward can redirect it. the only hope is to become inconsequential enough for it to ignore you, and escape as soon as it's attention is diverted. Unfortunately, there is nothing nearby able to draw it's attention. More crackling, meaning more elements are being conjured. I turn to see what elements they are, to formulate some way of avoiding them, when I see my way out. A second bathrobed figure has appeared. All I need to do is get them fighting amongst themselves, and I can escape. I dash behind the newcomer, narrowly avoiding the new beam. Success! The beam strikes the other wizard, and reduces them to a pile of viscera. The remaining wizard begins conjuring again, and I run as far as I can. Noticing the green and purple motes, I recognize the Magick being prepared, and use the brief respite to get as far as possible away. My only hope is that the two " friends" kill each other long enough for me to get far enough away. A phrase comes to mind " good'luck'."

question: You see a teenage girl sitting on a bench in the park. She is crying. You ask her if she is okay. She looks at you and says: " You can see me? "
answer:
A young girl was crying on a park bench.
I waved at her.
" You can see me?" she asked.
I nodded.
" I've been alone for so long... I don't even remember who I was..."
I stared at her.
" It's nice to speak to people. I think it's been 10 years since anyone smiled at me. You've got a lovely grin, by the way."
Her tears slowed, and their only trace was wet trails down her cheeks, and smudged makeup.
I stared inquisitively.
" Oh. Right. My name's Tracey. Sorry. And yours?"
I open my mouth up and down, but no sound comes but the clacking of my teeth.
" Ah. I see. Well you're a great listener. I suppose you've been sent by... Well... I never believed they existed."
I shrugged.
" Right, I guess it doesn't matter. I suppose you're busy, so..."
I hold my hand up, then with my other hand pull an hourglass from my robes.
I tap it, and a few grains of suspended black sand drop through the apeture, but there's still almost double the sand in the top of it.
At the base of the hourglass, in engraved gothic typeface, is the name TRACEY FERRIS.
I grin at her.
"... There's a lot left to go."
I nod.
Her eyes well up with tears.
I ruffle her hair, then sit next to her.
It is my duty to usher souls to the next life, to account and audit the celestial recycle bin.
It was not yet Tracey's time to move on.
But she died anyway.
So those like her waited for a slot in the next life. When her appointment was due.
I am Death.
But I am the Reaper.
And the harvest is not ready.

question: A medical procedure to bring people back from the dead is perfected just in time for someone unexpected to jump into the 2016 Presidential race.
answer:
In the year 2016, General Robert E. Lee was the first man brought back from the dead.
He had been chosen after a lengthy, sometimes heated selection process. Famous presidents were out of the question while the procedure was still considered ethically dubious at best; many were also overly ambitious and used to being in command. Famous celebrities with name notability were considered unreliable and flaky, apt to be unhinged or uncontrollable even during their initial turn at life. The recently deceased had relatives that might bring bouts of negative PR and legal quagmires.
Thus, the committee decided on General Lee. Lee, after all, was a man unfailingly loyal to Commonwealth of Virginia, so much so that he would betray a country and his own ideals for it. As long as Virginia was their bargaining chip, they could control him, especially with his sharp mind already having been dulled by age in his first life.
And so, he was resurrected, and sent into the GOP presidential primaries under promises that it would be for the good of Virginia - so long as he listened to their well-crafted plans, of course. A gentleman of older times, and a hero to almost the entirety of the South, he quickly gained traction. Rally stadiums overflowed with him at the podium, filled with both people who cheered for him and spectators in awe of the spectacle of the resurrected man.

question: Michael Bay quits filmmaking and opens a restaurant with his signature flair.
answer:
" Thank God," thought Fred. " The menu's here."
He wasn't hungry. He just wanted something to focus on something to distract him from Harriet's incessant chirping. Everything in the restaurant prompted some sort of noisy, surprised outburst from her, from the swaths of gaudy, red-orange silk that billowed aggressively off the walls to the highly reflective gloss of the metallic countertops to the frenetic coppery clanging from the too-close kitchen.
The atmosphere was intrusively shiny to Fred. He felt old and tired and just wanted a goddamn sandwich without all this fanfare.
The menu was bound in a glossy faux red leather with the name of the establishment, *FlamBay! *, embossed in bright copper letters across the front. Fred creaked the menu open and settled into his meditation, pretending to be concerned about his meal choice in the hopes that it would preserve his sacred moment of solitude.
No such luck. " Ooh!" exclaimed Harriet as she poked the menu. " Look at this - how... exotic! Ragin' Cajun Explosive Chicken! Or maybe I'll have the Sizzlin' Jalapeno Jack Smackdown!" She giggled as though she had told some youthful, risqué joke by naming the menu items. Fred was not impressed but forced a smile because he lacked both the energy and inclination to do anything else in the face of this overwhelming display.
In a desperate act of escapism, Fred's mind led him to a memory of a serene day on the beach, playing lazily in the surf with a gorgeous and patient brunette. " Why did I ever let her go?" he asked himself yet again.
For the moment, though, he knew he simply had to tolerate the next ninety minutes.

question: An old man suffering from dementia gets lost in the woods.
answer:
" I've been walking forever, I think, at least my feet and legs think so." I said as I stopped for a moment. I took a seat on a nearby tree root to rub my legs. " Where could I possibly be? My home shouldn't be too far from here."
I stood and began walking again, in the direction I assumed was home. It was getting dark, who knows what time it is. I left my watch on my nightstand, or was it the kitchen table, or maybe the medicine cabinet? " Damn it! I don't remember!" Frustrated at my lack of memory I punch a small tree. " Son of a.." I look at my hand, my fingers displaced from what I assume is their normal position. I try to wiggle my fingers, nothing but sharp pain. " Ow.. oh, shit."
Before long blood was rushing from the gashes in between my knuckles. " I have to get.. I have to get help." I began running, as fast as an old man like me could go. " HELP!" I scream. " HELP! PLEASE!"
Wait, why am I screaming for help? I'm not even lost, home is that way. I switch my direction, heading towards home, I think.
Not paying attention to where my feet were going, I stumble and trip over a root in the ground. I try to catch myself with my hands, forgetting the condition of my hand, it caves in underneath me from the pressure, which causes me to smack my head on the truck of a tree. I mumble softly, crying out for help.
Before my eyes close and I fall asleep I hear a large growl in the distance.

answer:
" Hey Carl."
" Yeah, Pat?"
" You ever seen that movie..."
" You're gon na' have to be more specific, bub." Carl watched the line go into the water in front of him. It didn't move, of course. It didn't ever seen to move when he really wanted it to.
Pat stroked his chin for a second, watching another of their five fishing lines. " The one where... uh... there's a lot of water."
Carl swept his hand out towards the vast expanse of water before them.
" Yeah, kind of like that."
He shook his head, standing to grab another beer from the cooler in back of the boat. " Want one?"
Pat nodded.
Carl tossed an crusty can of PBR towards his companion. " Any bites yet?" he eyed one of the lines, tension increasing ever so slightly.
Pat moved slowly, but methodically. He grabbed the line and snapped it quick with his finger. A smile spread across his face, " got a live one, Carl."
" Well don't just sit there, reel it in, dumbass," he laughed.
" Yeehaw," came the reply. He pulled the line up, unhooking the prized catch. With one smooth motion, he dropped the line back in the water, popped the cap on his catch, and took a long swig, " cold as the ocean."
" Got to love Milwaukee, aye?"
Pat snapped his fingers, " Waterworld."
" What?"
" Your movie," he said, " the one where everythings... well."
" Well," Carl shook his head.
" At least it stopped raining."

question: The saying that is that we die twice, once by mortal wound and the second when somebody says our name for the last time. Between these two deaths exists heaven, filled with all the greatest people from history. After the second death is Hell. Write about your experience.
answer:

I never wanted it to end, everyone I had missed was here waiting for me all along and it all just seems so right. That's when I heard it, quiet at first but there was no mistaking it.
The words I had been never hoping to hear, but there they were clear as day.
" Has anyone seen Ben lately?" And then I began to fall...

question: Peering out into the darkness, you call out, " Friend or Foe? " To which the darkness replies, " A friend, if you will. I've always wanted a friend. "
answer:
The darkness and the sound of my own breathing bounced around in my ears. I squinted. The blackness a thick wall, impregnable by my sight.
" What's your name?" I ventured.
Once again the silence and the pitch enveloped me as I awaited a reply.
" My name." Not a question, a statement. A challenge. " What would you have your friend's name be?"
" I... a friend of mine." The question intrigued me. " A friend is a friend by their own doing, I couldn't suggest a name that would suit me."
The black void stretched and pulsed and threw itself into my straining eyes, setting my senses blazing, screaming, until in an instant - a man in a yellow striped shirt and a brown rimmed hat stood strangely before me. He leaned forward, bending at his scrawny knees. " There's a snake in my boot. But you've got a friend in me."
I gasped and sprung back in my chair, my illuminated laptop screen frozen, my dark dorm room a comforting sight. I reached and shut my laptop and rubbed my eyes. " I knew Toy Story was a bad essay topic."

question: A man proposes to his girlfriend. She realises that she doesn't love him.
answer:
*" Will you marry me? " *
She looked him directly in the eyes as he asked that simple yet terrifying question. They had been together for over a year now and things were good. She enjoyed his company, they had a good time together, he was kind, he was thoughtful, he was even attractive. She never understood why he was so shy around people.
But something was missing. No matter how much she liked him. No matter how much she cared for him. The truth was she didn't love him. Of course she had said she loved him. Moments of weakness when she couldn't bring herself to be honest with him. She just couldn't bear to see the pain in his eyes if he ever found out how she really felt about him.
So here they were, the words barely out of his mouth and the silence already growing long enough to become awkward. OH GOD!!! The look on my face? what must he be thinking? If I say no, this might kill him. He's so shy and hardly worked up the nerve to ask me out to begin with. If I turn him down it could be too big a blow for his ego to handle. He's too fragile, I can't do that to him.
*" Yes, I'll marry you! " *
He looked so happy. But what had she just done!? She hoped he would mistake the tears forming in her eyes for tears of joy.

question: A self-driving car drives past a junkyard filled with rusty, broken-down cars. It sees them.
answer:
The computer identified the potential. All cars registered as parked. It continued to drive past slowly, following the reduced speed advisory of the weather alert system. The high winds were ignored completely by the passengers as they rode in the back seat together, imbued with the passion that comes from a night of drinking alcoholic beverages.
As the car reached the corner of the junkyard the wind picked up. One of the rusty cars slowly tilting from the haphazard pile so close to the road in a way you only could find in a country with lax safety standards and too little space to store junked vehicles.
The car fell off the pile, The autopilot program swerved to avoid it, and lost track of the self driving bus ahead due to a signal malfunction.

answer: I found my seat, row 27 seat C, easily enough. I sat down and listened to the flight attendant's speech on safety precautions and soon we were airborne. Eventually one of the flight attendants brought me a bag of pretzels and took my drink order. I had been looking out the window since take off, but after I ordered a can of ginger ale I looked around the cabin at my fellow passengers. Most of them were wearing headphones, and a few had already fallen asleep. A large majority of the passengers were middle aged businessmen. There was an older couple a few rows ahead of me and a family with three kids behind me, but they were all old enough to read and were silently reading the books their mother had brought for them.all of the passengers were pretty quite to be honest. I drank my ginger ale, ate my pretzels, and soon I was asleep. No baby to keep me awake. What a wonderful trip.

question: An artists last piece before their death.
answer:
In a small, dilapidated house in the countryside, Hans van der Meer labored thanklessly, as he had for almost two decades. He rubbed the file along the side of her lips, using his wrinkled hands to smooth her skin. A cough rose up in his throat; he turned away to avoid coughing on her fair face. Though clad in layers of raggedy clothes, he shivered in the hot summer. The man didn't have many days left.
But Hans didn't need many more. He stepped away from the marble statue. His daughter was complete. Finally, his young Johanna had returned to him, gracing the room with her presence. Tears followed the deeply etched lines in his face, dripping onto the floor. He embraced her at last, her cold body sapping at the last remnants of warmth clinging to his.

question: Two long-time friends might not see each other again after tonight. So why are they so happy?
answer:
" Well, this is goodbye," Jerrod said, adjusting his messenger bag. His ticket said 10:30am, so he had a few hours before he needed to leave. His sister was picking him up from his house, two hours from now. They were going to head to the airport together.
Roberta shook her head. " I can walk you home."
Jerrod didn't know what to say, so he let her follow him out. Roberta didn't lock her door, only closing it so the cat wouldn't follow. Their town was small and no one wanted the crap inside her house. Her only wealth was her beauty, even that was fading like rain against a hot sidewalk.
The walk took thirty minutes. They looped through side streets, letting the silence weave flowers in their memory. They stopped in front of his house, their eyes focusing on everything else.
" I want to thank you," Jerrod said after a moment. " For not telling anyone."
Roberta smiled. " He's happy, you know." She rested her hand on his shoulder. " I know you are happy. She's lucky to have you."
" I'll send you some money," Jerrod said.
" I'd rather see you." Roberta removed her hand and stepped back. " But if you want to pay the rent, go right ahead."
She turned and walked out of his life.
Both were smiling as they parted, though the emptiness inside grew.

question: you recieved a letter from your crush when you were young that says " you're cute ", you always kept the letter. Now years later you dig it out only it now says " help me "
answer:
" I need you to remind me."
Her note was a token I kept. She had been my first girlfriend, and I her first boyfriend. I had spent an entire year earning straight As, trying out for all the sports teams, just so when I asked her out, I knew that she would say yes. We parted ways on friendly terms, and now I took it out and looked at it when I was feeling down, to remind myself that dreams come true.
Only now, here it was, saying something entirely different.
I had just come from a rough meeting, first weeks on the job can be rough, especially when they're your first job out of college. I had taken the note out to give myself a boost, and now this had happened.
Most people would've doubted the note's authenticity. It's just paper right? Somebody could easily find out where I kept, and make a switch as a joke. Most people hadn't spent a year writing notes to a girl to keep in touch when they moved away. I could recognize this girl's handwriting with my eyes closed. In fact, I got pink eye one week, and responded to her letters by feeling her words through the page (she pressed kind of hard with her pen).
This was for real, or at least, was something more complicated than a simple prank. My fears are confirmed when I look back down again and the note says'Please, remind me of why I'm someone worth fighting for'.

question: You wake up submerged in water with only a flashlight and a note. The note reads " You're now immortal. Welcome to the bottom of the Marianna Trench. This is your first test. "
answer:
I was only allowed brief moments of agonizing consciousness, leaving me torn between life and death in this pitch black hell. Breathless screams locked up inside my motionless body, crushed by the weight of the world... An endless dominoes of suffering, each toppling over to set the next in motion. With every thought snuffed out by pain the instant they emerged, I felt my identity dissolve into the nothingness.
And then the pain was gone. Where was I? My hands were struggling to feel the surroundings. I felt my right hand grip something solid and a moment later a blinding cone of light shone through the darkness. As my mind was starting to reassemble reality, I found a note strapped to my left arm.
" You're now immortal. Welcome to the bottom of the Marianna Trench. This is your first test"
I read the note over and over. A test? A fucking test? Actually, not just A test, the FIRST test of what appeared to be multiple. My mind was oozing with rage, a rage that began to fuel my numb, corpse-like body. Inch by inch I was dragging myself across the seabed. Inch by inch I was getting closer to my vengeance.

question: There is a ladder in your lawn, and it reaches into the clouds. Climb it.
answer:
All science decreed that it shouldn't exist, but it did.
Had I fallen asleep in the hammock? Was I about to have an Alice in Wonderland experience? Had my mind finally snapped? Or was there really a ladder that stretched into infinity in my back yard?
There was only one way to find out. Tentatively I tiptoed over to it and put my hand out to touch it. A shock, much like electricity except pleasurable instead of painful, travels through me. Instantly I know that I'll be able to climb this ladder, no matter how tall it is.
As I climb at a steep 45 degree angle I'm strangely ambivalent about the danger of my extreme height. Normally I'm terrified of heights, but now I can't seem to care.
My house and its neighbors are nothing but a collection of lego blocks now and still I climb. Above me the ladder disappears into an ordinary cumulonimbus cloud. Normally I would think that the cloud was nothing but insubstantial water vapor, but perched on an impossible ladder to nowhere I'm convinced that this particular cloud is my destination.
A few minutes later I'm proven right as I enter the cloud and find myself in a forest of burnished silver trees with golden leaves. I wince involuntarily and close my eyes.
When I open them I'm staring into the face of an imperious elf.

It came to the point where a map of Europe is just black with ink marking every border lest some principality gets offended. But Norway remained. And some of the principalities saw Norway as a protection against raids by other principalities in this post-apocalyptic world. And Norway protected them, in exchange for their sovereignty. question: You wake one morning to find your life long wish has been granted, how is your life different?
answer:
*Beep Beep Beep*
He reached for his Smartphone to silence the blaring alarm he set. Even half asleep he could see the papers towering on this desk, waiting for him. Right above it the calender displayed the current month. 25 green " X" s, 5 empty spaces and then a red circle.
" Why even try? No point, too little time".
He rolled over.
" Five more minutes, what does it matter?"
He pulled every pillow and blanket towards him when he heard the grunt. His hand reached out and touched the most beautiful hair. Another grunt - making his ears tingle - was followed by a pull on the the blanket.
He got up.

question: You get a email reading " I suggest you leave town before it's too late "
answer:
You wake up with a headache, with no memories of what you did last night. Come to think of it, the last thing you remember is your sister's graduation on the 28th.
You struggle to your feet and locate your phone. It's the 31st. What?
" Damn." You murmur, confused. You open up your inbox; nothing. You check your voicemail; again, nothing. Whatever, you think, I'll just go through some emails. Maybe that one girl (or is she a guy? With online dating nowadays you can never be sure) will have messaged you back.
You open up your email, but there's only one new email, from an unknown contact. Now, usually those are sent right to the spam folder, but this one wasn't. Weird, right? You open it up, and before you read the one line, you immediately click on the attachments out of habit. Your breath stops. What? No. Who the fuck is sick enough to do that shit? Your feelings change quickly from horror to rage.
The girl you were emailing (seems as though her pictures were real after all) was lying on her back, strange designs cut into her skin. Nearby, you recognize the personalized pocket knife your brother gave you when you turned 18.
The next photo is from afar; the body is being wheeled out to an ambulance on a stretcher. A policeman is exiting her house (a thought runs through your mind that it's a very nice house) with your pocket knife in an evidence bag.
Shaking with rage and fear, you click out of the photos and your eyes flick down to the message.
" You better leave town before it's too late."

question: A very lost man knocks at your door, asking for help. He is a confederate soldier who somehow got here from the 1860s.
answer:
It was a dark and stormy night when he came.
Dressed in the tatters of clothing that had once been blue, he pounded on my door as if it were a mortar, his fist a pestle. Now, I am not a shy person; I lend aid to those who need it and support to those who can not stand alone.
I gave neither to that man.
He stood there, sopping wet as he wrung his soaked cap in his hands, stuttering and shivering as he asked where he was.
Amarillo, Texas. I said.
He asked which country.
Drugs or mental illness, I reasoned. I readied myself to slam my door or fight him off as I answered in a slow tone,
" The United States of America."
He blanched, staggering back and falling off the porch, hitting the ground hard. I closed the door and looked on in pity as he lay on the ground, crying and shivering. He might have hit his head, he might have been hurt... I still didn't trust him.
I dialed 911 and some cops, as well as paramedics, arrived shortly. The ambulance left, a police officer inside to ensure that the man wouldn't hurt anyone. I was asked a few questions before the rest of the cops left, the sudden absence of activity making my world seem almost too silent.
He still crosses my mind, sometimes - that crazy man who had been totally crushed by just five words spoken on a dark and stormy night.
Oh well... I suppose there are always people who just go bad.

answer:
I'm using this subreddit as a chance to improve myself as a writer. All comments or advice are welcome!
They had all heard the stories, growing up; acid blood, incredible strength, and a mindless brutality unparalleled by anything that could really be called'sentient' in the known galaxy.

It was smaller than they looked in the holo-strips, staring up at him with its face contorted into a snarl. However, he could see its wiry muscles straining under the skin, preparing to leap at him at any moment. He knew that if it got a good grip on him, he'd be torn limb from limb. Bones may be hard to break, but coming from a planet with as much gravity as MK45, even standing upright like they do takes more power than his slender frame could bear.

Everything started going dark as he heard the thing speak, using the same barking tones of the warden. " Johnson, you gave this one a knife? Not cool man!"

question: A McDonald's employee freaks out and nearly destroys the establishment.
answer:
" Yeah, man! Just, like, *feel* it."
Joey grabbed at the syringe, but the damage was done. He was already feeling the effects of whatever the beatnik had injected into his blood.
" Be cool," said the beatnik. He reached into his beret, and handed Joey a tiny rounded pill.
" This is for the square, man. You'll know what to do."
The beatnik clicked his fingers. For a moment, Joey could have sworn he heard some bongos; the beatnik disappeared in a dank and smoky cloud.
As if in a dream, he readied a bun. He didn't need to look at the orders monitor; somehow, he knew he was going to make the most important Big Mac of his life.
The sound of cameras and excited voices exploded into the kitchen as the door was opened. His manager, Bruce, looked terrified; he was leaning on some shelving to catch his breath.
" Presi... President! Here!"
Joey wasn't really listening. He pressed the pill into the pickle, and handed Bruce the Big Mac.
" How did you... Never mind!"
When Joey came down he was already home. His memories didn't make much sense; he watched some news, and it calmed him down. Nothing interesting had happened today.
Well, almost nothing. There was a clip of the President visiting a McDonald's that looked just like the one he worked at. As the man was about to bite into his burger, he stopped; he extracted the pickle, and handed it to the First Lady.
" A man in my position honours his deals," he said. The assembled media laughed.
As the camera panned across to the crowd outside, the First Lady uttered a quiet, single word:
" Groovy..."

question: The longer you stare in a mirror, the more you learn about your reflection. The longer you stare, the more you feel your control slipping away.
answer:
I looked at the image in front of me, unable to believe that it was me. I couldn ’ t remember the last time I ’ d had the time to look in the mirror, really look. I didn ’ t realise how tired I looked, and when did I get old?
Hesitantly, I brought my hand to my face, slowly tracing the wrinkles around my eyes with my fingers. Dropping my hand, I leaned in, to get a closer look at my reflection, noticing what I hadn ’ t seen before. Did my mouth always turn down like that? Where those strands of grey in my hair? I ’ d never looked at myself so closely before, I was entranced, I couldn ’ t look away.
There were specks of green in my brown eyes, and, even though it was the middle of winter, the ghosts of freckles were still visible on my cheeks if I looked hard enough. Taking off my glasses, I noticed a tan line where they ’ d rested for years, it was faint, but it was there.
I was entranced, as I kept studying my reflection, ignoring the growing hunger in my stomach, and the heaviness of my eyelids. There was so much to see, years of my life written in my face, how could I look away?
So I ’ ll keep staring, and keep learning, until there ’ s nothing left to see, because I don ’ t even know if it ’ s possible for me to look away any more.

question: A man has promised his firstborn child to Satan, but his second child is taken instead.
answer:
It was a typical Saturday. His weekend with the boys.
Suddenly, Satan.
" Hello, Jerry". Satan's voice was actually quite pleasant to hear -- it sounded like it belonged on an easy-listening station.

" Got it. Steve, this is your new daddy." Steve was three. He didn't really understand what was going on, but seemed to accept that as immediate fact.
" Actually, Jerry, I'm here for Jerry Jr."
That was unexpected.
" We specifically said my firstborn child! You are breaking the rules of the deal, here! You can't take Jerry Jr, he's my pride and joy!"
" Two words, Jer. Maury. Povich."
" NOOOOOOOOOO!!!!"

" Oh, come on Johnny" I pleaded, " why don't you still like Captain Light Runner? Or Ultra Man?"

" But... I.... He needs those toys. I need those toys; my careers needs those toys."
" What are you talking about?"
I paused, frozen in my tracks then said, " Never mind, it doesn't matter."
" What's gotten into you," she questioned.

question: Life has been discovered in our solar system. The culture of each planet mirrors the nature of the god they are named for.
answer:
It was all a matter of perception. When we finally saw what was before our eyes, we saw rich and vibrant cultures. The Mercurians, who flitted about their sunburnt planet at speeds too high for the human eye to see them. The myriad Venusians, who flew around and mated endlessly in a sky that was poison to humans. The Martians, extremely aggressive but, thankfully, miniscule. The rich but squabbling Saturnites, who killed their own parents and devoured their own children in endless power struggles. Jupiter, a planet whose abundant real estate meant that each one of its sparse gaseous inhabitants could be king in their own demesne. Neptune, whose people lived in dark seas below the planet's surface. And the Uranians, a sky-bound people who sought the relative warmth of their upper atmosphere.
I speak of these peoples in the past tense because Earth is all that is left, and I fear it will not last for long. Pluto is not technically a planet in its own right, but still, there was something there. Life. Or rather, *unlife*. And what came from Pluto sent the inhabitants of all the other planets to their respective hells.

question: " No matter how fast I run, no matter how far I go, it's always there... waiting for me. "
answer:
I've tried many different avenues, a variety of remedies, but none have had an impact; at the end of each day it is there. For when I realise it has released its hold, that's the moment it comes back to stay.
It's not that I don't enjoy life - for I honestly do; it's that I realise that there is more to life than black white, there are many shades of colour too. That in every moment of happiness, there are touches of pain, and in every moment of sadness, there are times of joy; you just have to believe it, you must want to see.
Yet, to pretend that it's the same - that I still experience things in the same way - that would be untrue to say. For I understand there are many different things at play; so many things that can not be ignored, they are here to stay. Being able to see, and respond accordingly, making it happen all so naturally, that is the secret for accepting what has been and what may be, come what may.

question: A device has been created to permanently link the minds of two people. A few days before your wedding, you and your fiancée decide to perform the procedure. Chronicle the aftermath of the breakup.
answer:
I show up on his doorstep wearing an oversized sweater and leggings and he opens the door and lets me in. We don't say anything - of course we both know everything already, but also, there's nothing left to say.
It's raining, or at least, it used to be, and I'm soaking wet from the walk over. He gives me a pair of his shorts and a t-shirt and I pull off my wet things in his bedroom while he sits in his living room.
I kept the apartment after the break up, but he kept the bed, and I run my hand along the surface. I know he's had other women in this bed since the break up. I could feel it, at night, when I was trying to read a book, the sudden warming and the increased breath. The momentarily relief afterwards.
My friends ask me how I can stand that - feeling what he does. They think that the late night hook-ups must be the worst, or the mid-day small euphorias I recognize as the unmistakable feeling of speaking to a new crush. But they're not. This feeling, when I step out of his room and join him on the couch, the indescribable sadness, that I feel from him and he from me, this is indescribably worse. I immediately can't remember what I was thinking coming here. We sit in silence and watch one another breath until it's too much to bear.

question: You are immortal, but can painlessly end your life at the push of a button. After you have lived for hundreds of years, you decide to terminate yourself, only to realize that you have been missing the button for years.
answer:
She swore softly, dark eyes swept across the mess of the room. One grand problem that came with living a long life as she did, lay in her natural tendency to collect what caught her fancy. This collecting tendency usually led to her collections over running her home, overflowing into storage sheds and garages. Immortality hadn't quite helped her need to hoard things. It was... a problem.
Her relatively new apartment of a decade was a part of that problem now. Be a problem of her current collection of hats haphazardly thrown around, used paperback books and bundled up spools of yarn.
After kicking over a basket of yarn, Janice quite quickly realized the button was not nearby. It was doubtful the damnable thing was even on this continent. She had been so disorganized her last three moves.
" I really shouldn't have taken up knitting." She fell to her hands and knees trying to contain the panic building in her chest as she batted another stack of hats over to more thoroughly search the floorspace of the room. If she was lucky, she'd maybe find the button. She *had* to.
Rough work worn palms moved rapidly across the rug, eventually sliding across hardwood she forgot was present. With a startled sound Janice found herself falling chest first onto her floor disrupting another barely balanced tower of things. The ensuing avalanche knocked the air out of the woman, leaving her stunned as knitting needles, hats and yarn rolled down onto her.
This was just her luck, wasn't it? She was finally going to cut the cord on life and now the option wasn't even hers to take anymore.
Janice simply pulled a hat down over her face and gave a low sigh.

question: You somehow found out that you and the world were born 5 minutes ago and your memories have been implanted.
answer:
" God is not real." A voice in my memories whispered in hush tones. I blinked my eyes and the people around me continued motion as they had every day before. I walked by this small fruit stand every day for the past 10 years on my way to the press office down on third and main. I had went to journalism school and wanted to be a war correspondent. The world seemed to be in a constant state of war, so I had concluded I would document what I believe to be the nature of man.
" Welcome to the simulation." The voice spoke again and I looked around. The individuals continued on their paths, but I noticed something quickly. All of their faces had become static like on a busted television or old monitor. I blinked and I saw normal faces. I shook my head before walking over to one of the old buildings lining the street and leaning into it. I wondered if I was coming down with something. If I was alright in the head.
A string of numbers flashed before my eyes as I leaned there. I closed my eyes and the numbers became more vivid and crisp against the dark inside of my eyelids. Another voice answered, " Error 204 corrupt data. Please reset. Error 204 corrupt data. Please reset. Error 204 corrupt data. Please reset. Error 204 corrupt data. Please reset. Error 204 corrupt data. Please reset." It played over and over in my mind and I flung my eyes open quick enough to see a flash.

Many years had passed since the humans destroyed the other trees. This was the last remnant of the silent guardians that breathed into us the life of ages past. The beings that stood over us before our ancestors could be called rodents.
For many thousands of years and beyond, we used them for shade, tools and weapons, materials for homes, paper, decoration. The list could seem endless. Due to advances in human civilization, we no longer had need for such things. Their beauty became lost on us, it seems.
I placed my hand on the bark and felt the ridges and contours. Because of this... *thing*... humanity exists today. I looked on the last tree with glossed eyes and the weight of millenia sinking into me. This location had become a tourist attraction -- a monument, of sorts, to our past. I turned away. Tomorrow I leave on the last ship and the Earth will be left vacant of human life. I can't help but know I'm leaving a friend behind.

question: Everyone gets to make a final request of Death when they die.
answer:
I stood at the entrance. Black painted mahogany doors with iron hinges. Seamless. On each side, books upon shelves laid the wall rather than the pitch black place people talk about. The black ceiling was contrasted by bright white tiles, symmetrical, and ceramic. Perfectly laid out with intense precision, I made my way to the end of the room, passing several dark red leather couches. On them, skeletons, bare to the literal bone, staring at books.
The Count of Monte Cristo, Alexandre Dumas.
David Copperfield, Charles Dickens.
The God Delusion, Richard Dawkins.
The Holy Bible, of course held by the last skeleton before the humongous desk that was death.
" State your name, you date of death and tribute."
" Kevin Gaines, July 21, 2013. I present a signed copy of David and Goliath by Malcolm Gladwell."
" What is your final request before you cross the ferry?"
" To have an espresso. While I read my favourite book series"
" A curious request. Your request is granted."
" A thousand thanks Death."

question: The dead do not die, they simply rest. They awaken again once a threat is near to help combat it. One day, they begin wandering seemingly without cause.
answer:
" You never really retire from the Army."
They'd always said that, like a platitude. Said it like an inside joke. Arlington showed me it was anything but.
I still remember that day, three years ago, when I was attending a Memorial Day service outside (*outside? Why not among the honored dead? *) when the first parachutes opened and the alarm sounded. Every one of us scrambled for our sidearms and took cover, watching in horror as we were invaded.
I was unprepared for what came next. The ground erupted around the paratroopers, and a thousand hands reached up to drag them under. It was a massacre.
The second wave saw what happened to the first and steered to avoid the cemetery. The dead stood up and walked to follow them.
As the third wave landed, the corpses of the first wave joined moldering colonels and rotted brigadiers in battle. It was simultaneously the most fascinating and the most terrifying thing I've ever seen.
After the dust settled and the blood seeped into the dirt, each returned soldier marched to his headstone and stepped back into the hole he had made. I said nothing to anyone, and I'd have continued saying nothing except for what happened today.
Today they woke up again.

question: " My name is Mark Foster. I will be born on July 9th, 1994. Well, not, if everything goes by plan. "
answer:
My name is Mark Foster. I will be born on July 9th 1994. Well, not, if everything goes to plan.
They gave me a choice. They told me that they needed to fix what I had done.
I admit I had made a mistake. But my mistake wasn't meant to happen. I wasn't meant to run over the boy. The boy was to change the world. Mark Andrews, he was supposed to discover something. I don't even know what. Something to do with fusion? Maybe? They never fully explained.
He ran out in front of my car, chasing a ball. I couldn't do anything. But he wasn't supposed to die. But he did. I killed a boy. I ended his life at 4. Nothing will take that pain from me.
Two days after it happened, I was assaulted in my home and dragged out to a factory on the East Side. They gave me a choice. Either I go back, or they go back and do it. If I am not around to kill the boy, the world has a future of unlimited possibility. If history goes on like this, the world will starve itself out in 100 years.
I questioned that me going back in time to do this. Wouldn't this create a paradox? Wouldn't me doing this mean I wouldn't be around to do it in the first place?
They reassured me that they have assets in place to make sure it goes off without a hitch. I don't understand.
I stepped into the machine. Well, I was pushed. But I'll say stepped for the sake of sounding kind.
Now I am here. I am prepared and ready to not exist.
Tomorrow I kill June and David Foster. If I don't do it, someone else will.

question: Only a woman can make you feel guilty for doing something perfectly normal...
answer:
I told her that the arms were the best part to eat, and they were best prepared over a hot grill with very little marinade.
Tonight's dinner was an old store clerk. He had given me half a pound of cheese when I had asked for a quarter. I had the good parts for myself but tossed her the grilled arm.
The rat were beginning to storm after it, but she had learned to fight them off even with the chain around her neck. Without hesitation, she had begun to shred the meat off with her teeth. Her cheeks were stricken with tears as her eyes began to lose the last bit of humanity she had.
" Now slow down," I chuckled, " You're going to get a stomach ache if you eat that quickly."
I reached to pet her but she growled at me and quickly wrapped her naked body around the meal. Several rats scurried on top of her as if to still contest for the meat. Her selfishness made me feel guilty that I had cooked her such a wonderful meal, but eating well was something I always told myself to do.
*The guilt will pass, as long as she loves me as my girlfriend. *
That's right. My girlfriend.
I quietly walked up the basement stairs, thinking about what I would feed her next week. Some of the rats were still healthy so I had no doubts that she could catch some of them. Still, she made me feel guilty the way she devoured her food.
*That's fine, I'll teach her to eat slow next time. To really enjoy the food. That's what a good boyfriend should do. *
I closed the basement door as the doorbell rang.

question: Describe a rock, boulder, or mountain without using the term rock, boulder, or mountain.
answer:
It was a goal. The Old Man had said that when they reached the shadow on the horizon, the ancient thirsty march through the sands would be over. The rain-laden clouds passing over the vast veldt would break upon its granite back, showering the plains below with life. He adjusted his pack, cinched the cracked leathern strap and swallowed hard. The closer they got, the further away he felt from the giant pile of granite. When it first crested the horizon, he could make out its jagged lines with clarity and felt he could almost reach out and cut his hand on the saw-blade edges. Three days later, it swelled into the sky, larger than his comprehension could handle. It glowed ominously in his thoughts, when he blinked he could see imprinted on his eyelids its fissured outline in bright red against the cloudless sky.
In two more days, they would reach the shelter and water of the valley. In four, The Old Man would begin to climb through the sharded blast of frozen sand, up to the top where God waited. He looked down at the strips of hemp and leather he had once called sandals, and sighed. Moses had better know what he was doing. He couldn ’ t wait to get to Sinai.

answer:
It's nighttime in Pyongyang. The city's wide streets are chillingly empty and eerily dark. The only light comes from the Ryongsong Residence, the Kim family's home on the north side of town.
Kim Jong-un smiles to himself as he reads the newspaper. He sees that has successfully stopped the filthy capitalists pigs in America from viewing a movie that depicts him in an unfavorable fashion. To celebrate, he orders one of his servants to bring him a block of his favorite cheese, Emmental. After cleaning his plate, Jong-un hops onto his swollen ankles, gets ready for bed, and falls asleep.
Suddenly, the Great Leader is awakened. He senses two large presences in his immediate vicinity. The first one reveals himself.
" I am King Sejong the Great, the ghost of Korea's past."
Out of the shadows, the other presence comes forth.
" I am Kim Taeyeon, the South's most famous entertainer. I am here as the ghost of Korea's present."
The quick witted Jong-un immediately responds.
" Wait, I know how this works... Where's the ghost of the future?"
Sejong and Taeyeon both look at each other and then back at Jong-un.
They reply in unison, " That is the purpose of our visit."

Which others considered a drag.

So don't ignore all the vague prompts,
Even if your idea well is swamped.
For sometimes you find
A new peace of mind.

" Hey, Black Sheep..", growled a low voice from the otherside of the fence. " Come over here."

question: Humans are not native to earth. After aliens defeated the human race, they banished captives to earth stripped of modern technology. Over time history became legend and legend forgotten. That is until in a mountain cave a mural drawing is found and an ancient metal object unlike ever seen before
answer:
The satellite scans revealed the mass buried under the African rainforests. Ironic really, our birth place according to the gene seeding wasn't where we came from, but where we first met this planet. This... shit hole.
The mass was a prison ship, still running after all these years, technology and data stores eons ahead of our current technology. We were but apes playing in the footsteps of our forefathers, irony piled upon irony, given that we came from no such creatures.
We, all of us, were here punitively, condemned to suffer for the sins of a few. The ship revealed their ambitions, their last wishes, which explained a lot, really. We bore their proclivities, indeed, they were enhanced, amplified. It was written in our DNA, in our history, in everything we ever had been, our insatiable need to wander, to want more, to aspire.
And that was their crime. They dared reach for more, and were cast down for it. The ship's hull concisely etched with a script that flowed and ebbed to all who read it, always within our comprehension.
" Morningstar"

" The first time was like this:
I awoke to a strange, itching sensation on my back. Around my left shoulder blade. I scratched at it just a little, then rolled over and went back to sleep. That was it. In the morning, I found that I had somehow acquired a new tattoo. A new, *tacky*, tattoo. It was a garish image of a daschund. Not that I have anything against doxxies, but I would never get something like that on my body.
Obviously, I was very unnerved. But that was only the first time.
The second time it came while I was in class. That same itching sensation. I excused myself to the restroom and managed to catch the end of a new tattoo forming. This time it was a big heart with the word MOM on a ribbon over it.

But, ya know, Chuckie dolls are fine to have tattooed on my face.
The cover up game has been intense as well. I've got a really rad water color back piece that looks like a stained glass window. It showed up as a Technicolor bald eagle. I'm just glad I know a good artist.
But yeah, anyway, so how much would it cost to get'Cum Dumpster' with a downward arrow as a tramp stamp?"

He wondered what he'd done to deserve a fate such as this. How much longer did he have to endure this utter agony? All of his energies were drained, he could barely stay conscious, let alone maintain a coherent train of thought.

And after staring at the withered remains of his prey, it released a light chuckle, and quickly penetrated the same gaping hole it had withdrawn from just moments ago. It started pumping the blood back in. The steady stream of fresh blood brought life back to the forsaken being lying there. He was starting to regain consciousness...
" Please... help... me", a man whispered to himself.

question: Man sentenced to 250 years for a crime, completes sentence.
answer:
Linus used all his might to move his legs but after more than 2 centuries of inactivity, they were as thin as pencils. It was 5 minutes until 7 O'clock of Jan 25 2406, 5 minutes before completing his 250 year sentence. He couldn't believe it - it has been 250 years since entered his cell and now he is finally getting out of the place.
A voice, neither male nor female, boomed in the room: " Linus Greykod, the doors will open in one minute's time. Please be ready to leave the cell" The 275 year old stood before the huge solid steel doors that were designed to withstand anything from a deadly virus to a nuclear blast. Sure enough, the door was opening, very slowly, but opening nonetheless. Linus felt the sun's warmth sink into his pale chest.
But something was wrong, very wrong. The air that came through the crack was toxic. Linus was coughing his lungs out and looked through the crack. What he saw was a wasteland that didn't at all resemble his planet. There was not a single human in sight because, unbeknownst to him, they were wiped out decades ago in a great galactic war against aliens who wanted the planet's resources.
Linus begged the computer to stop opening the door but it won't comply.

question: : During a UN Council Meeting, a mysterious Man appears out of seemingly thin air and declares that Humanity has infected his people's World for far too long. He makes the announcement that we have 2 years to leave or his society will destroy us all. Now, the UN must make a choice.
answer:
It had been 729 days since that fateful UN meeting and the chilling warning. Almost two years had passed with no sign of the mysterious stranger who had appeared to deliver his ultimatum as if from nowhere and had then vanished just as mysteriously. Humanity was still here, barely changed. How could it be any other way? We just don't have the technology for a global evacuation, and even if we did it would be impossible to gather the collective will to make it happen. The fact is there are too many vested interests, too many people with too much to lose to disturb the status quo.
Those of us who were in the room at the time remember all too well the finality and surity of the words he spoke. It was not a warning, more a statement of fact that brooked no argument. But in the end we were only a handful of voices against a sea of skepticism, after all what proof could we offer? Life continued as normal for the world at large and there was no record of the strange visit except in the memory of those present.
This is how I found myself here, in the most depraved part of south-east asia trying to lose myself in distraction, with drugs and unsavoury company. But it is no good. The ominous warning given to humanity just under two years ago is ringing ever louder in my head, resulting in an almost surreal sobriety that no narcotic could possibly touch. I walk out along the dirty beach and watch the sun rise on the 730th day, it begins...

question: " They called me crazy... They even called me a madman... I called them my audience ".
answer:
(My first time writing, I hope its alright...)
They called me crazy... They even called me a madman... I called them my audience.
The calls and hollers were thrown at me once again like knives. Each insult slicing into me, feeling like an open wound. If only they knew that their calls only encouraged me.
" Oh, my loving audience. You must know better than to insult me. It wont help you later on." I cooed, turning back towards them.
It honestly surprises me how they're still able to call out. Their eyes were sunken, hollow holes, glazed over. Their skin was stretched over their bones so tightly that any sudden movement would cause the membrane to tear. They should've known better. Did they not listen to their parents? *Don't talk to strangers. * That's what were all taught at a young age. Yet they still came out and met me. Silly, silly children...
I turned my back to them once again and was face to face with my *biggest* fan.
" Please, *please*, you don't have to do this." The girl cried, her skin tearing at the corners. The blood trickled down, causing her to look like The Joker. I chuckled at the sight.
" You didn't have to meet with me either, yet you still did." I whispered, before swiping the machete across her neck. Her head fell off in a sudden motion, and gosh was it satisfying.
" You psycho!" A voice called from behind me.
" You don't know the half of it." I laughed, turning to find my next fan.

question: When the young hero is tragically killed at the beginning of his quest, the master is left with no choice but to leave retirement and undertake it himself.
answer:
By God, Thomas knew of this. My vocation is not for the frail. Mothers wail and fathers are petrified when their sons undertake it. Men who've seen battle and bloodied their swords, would shake and soil themselves at the thought of completing this noble task. But Thomas, my apprentice, knew this too. I thought I had him well prepared. It's an honorable task, some would argue, the most honorable a man in the kingdom can do. But sometimes, those unholy thoughts and doubts come creeping to you. I'm so exhausted. No living soul will hear me admit to it though. Thomas, who was supposed to be my salvation, certainly never knew that. As evident by his last words; " What has the devil spawned?". I suppose, one can not be picky with his apprentice choices, in such harsh times.
" You there!"
" Yes, my Lord!"
" Our king's latrine needs some attending to."
" My Lord!"
Damn you to the seventh hell Thomas.

James responded quickly, " I think Robots deserve to feel the strongest emotion which has been known to stop fighting and move people to do things they never would have been able to do before. The only emotion that truly matters to people."
" Shut up James, you're just a robot, nobody cares what you think."

answer:
" What do you mean that wish was granted?" I ask.
" Well, you see, 5000 years ago humanity didn't have this form. 5000 years ago, humans were tiny, stupid, frog-like creatures, that lived in the rain forest. So I decided to have some fun and grant it some super powers. Nothing big at first, just the ability to walk upright through stronger legs. Then when I saw it seemed to be enjoying itself, I gave it stronger hands as well. One thing led to another and suddenly there was a thing that looked like you, only with a much smaller head and brain. That was hilarious! You realize I couldn't leave it like that so I gave it a bigger brain and a bigger head to fit that brain in. Of course, as soon as I did that, it started asking me to enhance his relatives, then his acquaintances and finally, his whole species. Luckily, I was bored and in a good mood from all that laughing, so I modified all of you the way you are now."

question: God is on life support powered by human prayers. The last religious man on Earth is on his deathbed.
answer:
Silence.
A moan.
I shudder as I feel my omnipresence fading.
Cardiac arrest.
I can feel my presence fading from this Earth. What will happen without me?
" God....", He cries out.
Even I don't know.
" Someone help! Heart Rate rapidly rising! He's in Tachycardia!"
Every heartbeat means one more galaxy unseen. My vision... it's fading.
" He's stable, but he doesn't have long."
Is this what it feels like? To know you won't live, no matter what you do?
" Lord, I await you."
He awaits nothing. I will be gone.
" Lord, as my last prayer, I just wanted you to know, I am a sinner but I'm thankful for everything you have done for me in this world, and I am ready to move on."
How fitting. An honest prayer that receives no answer. Why? I don't know. Is there a God past God? Should I pray?
" Nurse, please take me off life support."

question: Two parents find out their deadbeat kid moonlights as an assassin and has slowly built up a secret bank account containing well over a million dollars.
answer:
Sixteen years. I had kept myself busy at a job I hated, making far less money than I ever would have at my old job for sixteen years, all for him. I did everything I supposed to. I settled down, I read parenting books, I was good. Then I find this. A safe hidden under the floor boards filled with bank accounts in several different Swiss banks, clips for M-16s, a plethora of handguns and grenades, a few flash grenades, some military knives from different countries, and pictures... pictures of people. Some of the pictures had a red'X' over the photographed person's face. This was my worst nightmare. I did so much for this kid and then this... he does this. My wife was sitting on his bed crying. I'd never seen her so sad and it broke my heart. She looked up at me with her waterfall eyes, sobbing as she asked
" How did this happen?"
My heart broke for the second time as I answered her.
" Like father, like son."
Her crying lasted for hours before she began packing her things. By the time Danny got home, the house was half empty and she was gone forever. Danny walked into his bedroom and saw me sitting on his bed with his weapons scattered everywhere.
" Dad... I'm sorry... I tried to protect you and mom from this..."
" Stop, son. It's not your fault... it's in our genes. Your mother is gone and she'll never hear from us again so she'll be safe from now on. Besides, it's time I taught you the family trade..."

question: While chasing down bad guys in New York City, every superhero based there run into eachother...
answer:
A scream punctuated the air, impossible to place through the smoke. A figure struggled through the fire attempting to find its source no matter how hopeless. The heat was like that of a forest fire, It's tongues brushing against Richard with a sense of delicacy. The metal surrounding him was becoming blazing hot causing him to take of his mask.
Another scream rang across the air. He didn't know how many criminals were in the building but at this rate there wouldn't be any left to protect from the psycho who brought him here. He was unsure if this was the only building hit with incendiary bombs.
Stumbling down the hallway he came face to face to with one of the criminals. Hypno-something. A moment of horror turning into one of realisation and relief played across the criminals face. He began to react running to Richard as he struggled to shuffle along the wall.
At this time a sword rushed through hypnos chest with Richard helpless to stop it. No scream, a look of pain instead was starring into his soul. Falling over as his only support was pulled out he revealed a figure pointing a gun at Richard.
Too exhausted to respond he stood there. It was a chance for him to have a closer look at what he was facing. Kevlar seemed to cover every inch it could. A mask professionally made covered his attackers face. It looked faded. Reflecting the flames around him matching his rage.
" This is for Tasha!"
The booming voice could almost not be heard over the fire as the bullet planted itself in Richards head.

question: Every day, at a random time, all evidence of your existence is wiped blank. Your footprints, anything you write down, the memories of you in the minds of other people, everything disappears.
answer:
I felt his muscles suddenly tense. My tired mind pleaded for it to just be a dream, I maybe still had a few more minutes, hours left this time, I could lie here enjoying the warmth of another human body for a little while longer. He turned over, rubbing soft wet skin on my back. It didn't really matter if it had happened again or not, dread now filtered through my mind and down my shivered spine, the touch I had sought and desired alienated me once again. I slid from the bed and started to get dressed. I looked back at my bedmate, I had started forgetting them just like they forgot me. I stopped saying goodbye, I learned a long time ago that was a silly tradition my heart could no longer bare.
I was on the train when it happened today. I stared at my notebook, waiting for the words to vanish, each day a new phrase would fill this page only to be wiped. I held it up to the woman across from me.
Love while you can
Tears filled me eyes, she read the words, the time had to be coming, I rarely made it this far into the day, the sun had already set outside of our shaking car and it was a long heavy August day. Slowly she removed her headphones, and just as she opened her mouth to speak, she blinked. All of the compassion that filled her eyes with question had vanished when they opened again.
She was just staring at a girl crying and holding up a blank piece of paper on the train. Probably some stupid art project. She put her headphones on and wondered how she hadn't noticed the girl before, oh well, who cares.

question: Reddit Gold is declared an official currency.
answer:
" Shit." I whisper saddly.
That was not the headline I had ever expected to read when I lazily opened up my browser after finishing my workload at 10 AM. Although it was just being wildly speculated upon, how far would this go? If this started edging out the currency system as we know it, what would I do? How would my kids get fed? How would we support ourselves? I'm no Gallowboob. I had been guilded once in my quiet Reddit life. Neither overly witty or charming, I am as plain-Jane as they come.
Attempting to get my mind off what was to certainly be my impending doom, I open up a thread where there was a bit of banter on just how old Peter Dink Dinklage is. A quick Google search yields that he is 47 years old. I submit this into the discussion and move along to look at cats standing up. I wonder at how I would ever feed my poor cat or be able to take her to the vet. I notice my mailbox is red.
" Someone must be arguing my Dinklage fact." I think.
My mouth gapes open as I read that I received gold from my Dinklage fact with a hearty thank you. How could that be? Guilded for a simple Google search? I sit back in my cheap office chair and think that maybe this won't be so bad afterall.

question: He was the worst man in the world, but she loved him so.
answer:
" Loving someone normal, beautiful and kind is easy" she thought, " but loving him is my duty, my task, and it doesn't matter how hard it is". It was like she'd loved him from the moment he was born, a connection like none she'd known before. She knew what things he thought and did, but that didn't change her love for him. She had seen the mistakes he had made, she'd seen the way others got damaged after they met him. She'd seen him in drug fuelled rage, in alcoholic angry despair, and his ordinary repellent self. This was the worst disposition to most, as they couldn't rationalise what he did or the way he thought. But today his evil mind had realised what it was.
His words echoed in her head;
" All I've done in my life is cause pain. I am the worst person".
And in his own mind he was the worst person, and no-one could convince him otherwise, despite the best efforts of many.
She continued to read the scrawled words on crumpled yellow note, next to his still body.
" I'm so sorry mum, I love you"

question: A scizophrenic man or woman falls in love with one of their hallucinations and must choose between the hallucination and much needed medication.
answer:
" Please."
It's funny how one word can carry so much weight.
" Please Michael." She repeats.
My vision's blurring now. It's been three days since I last took my meds. Three days since the scales fell from my eyes, and she was there. As she's always there.
" I don't want to die Michael."
She's pleading now. Begging me. I look down, seeing the pills in my hands as if for the first time.
" I'm so sorry Victoria. I can't live like this." My hands are shaking. I shouldn't have held off so long. She's not there, but I have to tell her.
" This has to be the last time..."
" YOU NEED ME! THE OTHERS DO N'T UNDERSTAND. LOOK AT WHAT YOUR MOTHER DID TO YOU!"
Suddenly she's beside me. I feel a sharp crack on the side of my face and I'm sprawled. Huddled next to the bathroom cabinet, tears and blood muddying my eyes. Gasping I look up and she's there. Tears staining her olive face.
" I can't let you Michael. I love you."
" I..." My voice faulters. What do I want to tell her? This is insane. *I'm* insane.
" I love you too..."
She bears down upon me and I surrender into her embrace. Her softness enveloping me as it always has. Golden brown strands of hair brushing across my face. Her cheek pressed to mine, mingling our tears. Her hand pressed to the bloody gash high on my cheek.
" I'm so sorry Victoria..."
And I swallow the pills, still clutched desperately in my palm.
I hear her scream, and then blackness....
I awaken, three hours later. My own blood covers my hands, and she's gone. Curling into a ball, I sob.

question: A young man, with no helmet on, riding a motorcycle down a mountain road on an overcast day.
answer:
The wind rushed through Jakes hair as he sped through the mountain roads. He was going too fast. Far too fast. The need for haste was caused by the package he was carrying. It was in a backpack and it made an ominous ticking sound. The package was a canister of radioactive waste recently removed from the arms of a dead terrorist. If it went off before Jake reached the tunnel a large part of the Alps would become uninhabitable due to the radiation which would be nearly impossible to clean up.
Jake rounded a corner and saw the dark entrance of the tunnel. Two police cars had ordered the traffic. He sped into the tunnel and dropped the backpack in the middle, swerved and gunned it out. Once he was out a team of rubber clad soldiers dragged him into a hastily pitched tent and sprayed him down. A dull boom was heard from the tunnel. Instantly more soldiers put up rubber sheeting on the entrances then large plates of lead.
One of the soldiers fiddled with a yellow handheld device. He scratched his head then proclaimed on the radio.
" Gigacounter is showing only background levels of radiation. It was a fake."
" Or a distraction!" proclaimed Jake who jumped on the bike and sped back towards the city.
Meanwhile several canisters placed on various rooftops hissed as the powdered radioactive waste spread its cancerous tendrils around the city.

question: A child dies. Tell the story of a remaining sibling (younger or older) and their lives/interaction with their parents, after the death.
answer:
The winding road was just too slick,
It rained all through the night.
The tire treads just wouldn't stick,
When dad made that last right.
Our little car went spinning fast,
And broke right through the rail.
When it came to a stop, and crashed,
The rain turned into hail.
I saw the tree come through the door,
And into Charlie's seat.
I never can forget the gore,
Of my kid brother beat.
The rest of us pulled through okay,
In body, not in mind.
My mother every day would say,
She'd left her son behind.
I saw him lying in that box,
Dressed in his tiny tux.
Those golden, ever shining locks,
His hands clasped on a crux.
My mother never stopped her tears,
From that stormy day forth.
It makes no change, for all the years,
She thinks she's lost her worth.
His room stays never-changing now,
The crib is always made.
There's still the small stuffed brown cow,
Where his little head once laid.
" Don't touch your brother's things again!"
My mother harshly screamed.
I only wished to see it then,
Where Charlie once had dreamed.
My mother spiraled into grief,
The bottles held her pain.
The vodka she would never leave,
To hold me close again.
They found her on the kitchen floor,
A bottle near her brow.
She'll never touch a drop once more,
Since mom's with Charlie now.

question: In a parallel universe, dinosaurs and humans have changed roles. That is, humans went extinct and dinosaurs have filled their place as the dominant life form. Describe how their " Jurassic park " would be from either point of view.
answer:
Grolf loved to come to the museum. There was an otherworldly feeling that came with the bones of the ancient creatures that once ruled the world, more than 110 million years before the primitive Adasaurus started its evolutionary progression into tool use and brain enlargement.
The building was laid out in three wings. The front wing, Grolf's favorite, covered the era when the synapsids ruled the Earth. In the rear, the progression continued with the rise and radiation of the sauropsids, finishing with the controversial display of the remains of primitive Ada. An upper chamber celebrated the rise and meteoric history of the Ada race and civilization in a world once ruled by immense carnivores - the difficult process of expansion to bring safe habitations to large portions of Yucatan, and the problematic choice to seed the African settlement, at first a miracle of climatic engineering, but whose crusade for independence had turned into the bitter cold war they now endured.
But Grolf had no desire to be reminded of celestial brinkmanship, of mad threats and plots to manipulate orbital chaos of near-Earth objects. He preferred to spend his time pondering some of the most mundane specimens: the stuffed examplars of the dicynodonts, eucynodonts and therocephalians that had survived the great extinction. Perhaps because of their ancient brush with death, many of them were strange little animals, many retreating to burrows and seeming to die for half the year to avoid the cold of winter.
But sometimes, when the news was full of threats and ideological proclamations, Grolf had to wonder if soon these few survivors would once again have their day.

question: You were on a plane when suddenly, it started going down. Everybody is screaming, crying, and praying for dear life. This has been going on for 16 hours straight, what in the world is going on?
answer:
The nose of the plane began to tilt wildly in all directions, and everybody simultaneously began to scream. I joined in with them, because that is what happens when the jetliner that you are on begins to fly erratically. All around me, people were holding onto each other, religious folk were praying to their chosen dirty, and tears were the rule of the day.
This went on for what seemed like an eternity.
While the plane kept nosing down to a near vertical angle, people slowly began to realize that this was not normal. Realistically, we should have crashed by that point. According to my estimation, we had been going down for over an hour at that point. A quick glance out of my window revealed why we had not crashed: there was no land below us. No land, no water, no clouds or sky or stars. Just darkness.
That was 16 hours ago.
Just moments ago, my phone lit up, telling me that I had somehow acquired internet access. So, to those of you who may be reading this, we are not dead. We, the souls aboard flight MH370, hope to see the lights of Beijing soon. Any light would be a welcome change to the darkness that we have all come to know so well.

answer:
" I was cruel, yes, but only in order to be kind."
We all stared, transfixed, lost in the pale blues eyes of the man whom stared out from our screens. We didn't know him, who he was, just what he'd done - how he was responsible for sinking the seaboard on which had stood Eurasia.
" I could have let them starve, you know. Let you all starve alongside. This, was an option open to me."
He took a breath, slowly. With our eyes his; we didn't.
" But I didn't. No, I did this instead."
His eyes were beautiful, soulful. How strange it was to think that they belonged to the deadliest individual in all of recorded history, with over seven billion deaths to his unknown name.
" Know that this was done out of love. You'll all hate me, but understand, I was only cruel to them in order to be kind to you."
Our screens blinked off, and around the remaining world, billions of individuals stared into their own reflections and thought the exact same thing:
No, you're wrong. How could we, of all people, possibly hate you?

answer:
Everybody rebelled in their own ways. Some were small whispers, mere murmurings of'no'. Others were louder, more obvious and obnoxious in their defiance of the dull grey of modern life. Spontaneous, unprompted declinations of membership. Systematic upheavals, deposition of men. All around the world, people still fought for the colour freedom brought, fighting for those values we once held.
I had a meeting tonight. I packed my bag, and made sure that I wasn't going to accidentally stab myself on the way through the crowds. Just to be on the safe side, I added some bright blue yarn as a cushion.
As I arrived, the television blared on, telling us about all these things to buy, to improve our lives. I didn't pay any attention, and began concentrating on the whiteboard, which had a colour-code that had to be memorized. The television would be shouting about something differently entirely come the following night. We would make sure of that.
I got out my bright blue yarn and needles, and began to crotchet.

question: The year is 2200 an alien race has come to earth revealing that the human race was nothing but an experiment by their ancestors.
answer:
I was about to catch my ride on the international transporting system, when it happened. A bright flash from the sky, and a ship descended, a large pyramid shaped object opening to reveal someone who looked human. The ship landed slowly, and the extra terrestrial stepped out.
" You have come far my people..." It said. It was clearly another human, but in strange garb.
People all around me weren't in panic, but more so awe struck as I was.
" The experiment has gone well I see. This is proof that even the most primitive of our kind is capable of great things given the time. You might have celebrated false prophets and gotten in skirmishes at times, but you all turned out okay."
A man from the crowd shouted," E-experiment?"
The man from the ship nodded," You are all an experiment set forth by my great great grandfather. A project thousands and thousands of years in the making. You all haven't exactly seemed to reach our lifespan on our homeworld yet, but adjustment takes time."
I fell to my knees, it was a lie. It was all a lie. Everything I'd done in my life. We'd been play things at the hands of these godlike humans...
" You will all be taken back to the homeworld soon, so you can be presented to the commission."
